title.zh: 卷五十五 吳書十 程黃韓蔣周陳董甘淩徐潘丁傳
title.en: Volume 55: Book of Wu 10 - Biographies of Cheng, Huang, Han, Jiang, Zhou, Chen, Dong, Gan, Ling, Xu, Pan, and Ding
title.raw: 卷五十五 吳書十 程黃韓蔣周陳董甘淩徐潘丁傳 Volume 55: Book of Wu 10 - Biographies of Cheng, Huang, Han, Jiang, Zhou, Chen, Dong, Gan, Ling, Xu, Pan, and Ding

sentences.zh: 程普字德謀，右北平土垠人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Pu, courtesy name Demou, was a man from Tuyin in Right Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Pu, styled Demou, came from Tuyin in Right Beiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 初爲州郡吏，有容貌計略，善於應對。

translations.literal: At first he served as a clerk in provincial and commandery government; he had a striking appearance and strategic sense, and was skilled in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a provincial and commandery clerk—presentable, shrewd, and quick in debate.

sentences.zh: 從孫堅征伐，討黃巾於宛、鄧，破董卓於陽人，攻城野戰，身被創夷。

translations.literal: He followed Sun Jian on campaigns, attacked the Yellow Turbans at Wan and Deng, defeated Dong Zhuo at Yangren, assaulted cities and fought in the field, and his body was wounded in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned under Sun Jian: against the Yellow Turbans at Wan and Deng, against Dong Zhuo at Yangren, taking towns and fighting in the open until his body bore battle wounds.

sentences.zh: 堅薨，復隨孫策在淮南，從攻廬江，拔之，還俱東渡。

translations.literal: When Jian died, he again followed Sun Ce in Huainan, joined the attack on Lujiang, captured it, and then crossed east together with him.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Jian died he followed Sun Ce in Huainan, helped capture Lujiang, then crossed to the east with him.

sentences.zh: 策到橫江、當利，破張英、于麋等，轉下秣陵、湖熟、句容、曲阿，普皆有功，增兵二千，騎五十匹。

translations.literal: When Ce reached Hengjiang and Dangli, he defeated Zhang Ying, Yu Mi, and others, then advanced to take Moling, Hushu, Jurong, and Qu'e; Pu had merit in all of this, and his troops were increased by two thousand men and fifty horses.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengjiang and Dangli Ce broke Zhang Ying and Yu Mi, then rolled through Moling, Hushu, Jurong, and Qu'e—Cheng Pu distinguished himself throughout and received two thousand more soldiers and fifty horses.

sentences.zh: 進破烏程、石木、波門、陵傳、餘杭，普功爲多。

translations.literal: Advancing, he broke Wucheng, Shimu, Bomen, Lingzhuan, and Yuhang; Pu's achievements were the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In the push that took Wucheng, Shimu, Bomen, Lingzhuan, and Yuhang, Cheng Pu's contribution was foremost.

sentences.zh: 策入會稽，以普爲吳郡都尉，治錢唐。

translations.literal: When Ce entered Kuaiji, he appointed Pu as Commandant of Wu commandery, with his seat at Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ce took Kuaiji, Cheng Pu became chief commandant of Wu commandery, based at Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 後徙丹楊都尉，居石城。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to be Commandant of Danyang and resided at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was later shifted to commandant of Danyang and established his headquarters at Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 復討宣城、涇、安吳、陵陽、春穀諸賊，皆破之。

translations.literal: Again he campaigned against the bandits at Xuancheng, Jing, Anwu, Lingyang, and Chungu, and defeated them all.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again against bandits in Xuancheng, Jing, Anwu, Lingyang, and Chungu and routed every band.

sentences.zh: 策甞攻祖郎，大爲所圍，普與一騎共蔽扞策，驅馬疾呼，以矛突賊，賊披，策因隨出。

translations.literal: Once Ce attacked Zu Lang and was greatly surrounded; Pu, with a single rider, together screened and defended Ce, drove his horse and shouted sharply, thrust at the bandits with his spear, the bandits scattered, and Ce thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Ce besieged Zu Lang and was nearly encircled, Cheng Pu and one companion shielded him: charging forward with a battle cry, he speared into the enemy ranks until they broke and Ce broke free.

sentences.zh: 後拜盪寇中郎將，領零陵太守，從討劉勳於尋陽，進攻黃祖於沙羨，還鎮石城。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General of the Household Who Sweeps the Bandits (middle rank), concurrently Prefect of Lingling; he followed the campaign against Liu Xun at Xunyang, advanced to attack Huang Zu at Shaxian, then returned to garrison Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was named middle general who sweeps bandits and acting prefect of Lingling, fought Liu Xun at Xunyang, struck Huang Zu at Shaxian, then returned to hold Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 策薨，與張昭等共輔孫權，遂周旋三郡，平討不服。

translations.literal: When Ce died, together with Zhang Zhao and others he assisted Sun Quan, then operated across three commanderies, pacifying and subduing those who would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: After Ce's death he assisted Zhang Zhao in counseling Sun Quan, rode the three commanderies, and forced every holdout to yield.

sentences.zh: 又從征江夏，還過豫章，別討樂安。

translations.literal: Again he followed the expedition to Jiangxia; on the return he passed through Yuzhang and separately campaigned against Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Jiangxia expedition, then on the way back moved through Yuzhang and separately reduced Le'an.

sentences.zh: 樂安平定，代太史慈備海昏，與周瑜爲左右督，破曹公於烏林，又進攻南郡，走曹仁。

translations.literal: When Le'an was pacified, he replaced Taishi Ci in guarding Haichun, and with Zhou Yu served as left and right commanders-in-chief; they defeated Cao Cao at Wulin, then advanced on Nan commandery and drove off Cao Ren.
translations.idiomatic: With Le'an quiet, he relieved Taishi Ci at Haichun and shared joint command with Zhou Yu: they shattered Cao Cao at Wulin, pressed into Nan commandery, and drove Cao Ren away.

sentences.zh: 拜裨將軍，領江夏太守，治沙羨，食四縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Major General Who Supports the Army, concurrently Prefect of Jiangxia, with his administration at Shaxian and revenue from four counties.
translations.idiomatic: He became supporting major general and Jiangxia prefect, administering from Shaxian with income from four counties.

sentences.zh: 先出諸將，普最年長，時人皆呼程公。

translations.literal: Among the generals who had gone out before him, Pu was the eldest in years; people of the time all called him Lord Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Of the commanders who had served longest, he was senior in age, and everyone called him "Lord Cheng."

sentences.zh: 性好施與，喜士大夫。

translations.literal: By nature he loved to give alms and delighted in gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous by nature and enjoyed the company of educated men.

sentences.zh: 周瑜卒，代領南郡太守。

translations.literal: When Zhou Yu died, he succeeded as concurrent Prefect of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhou Yu's death he took over as acting prefect of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 權分荊州與劉備，普復還領江夏，遷盪寇將軍，卒。

translations.literal: When Quan partitioned Jingzhou with Liu Bei, Pu again returned to hold Jiangxia; he was promoted General Who Sweeps Away the Bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan split Jingzhou with Liu Bei, Cheng Pu went back to Jiangxia, rose to full rank as general who sweeps bandits, and died.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：普殺叛者數百人，皆使投火，即日病癘，百餘日卒。〉

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: Pu executed several hundred rebels, had them all thrown into fire, and the same day fell ill with plague; after more than a hundred days he died.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu adds that he threw hundreds of traitors into the flames, fell ill that same day with pestilence, and died some hundred days later.

sentences.zh: 權稱尊號，追論普功，封子咨爲亭侯。

translations.literal: When Quan assumed the imperial title, he posthumously assessed Pu's merit and enfeoffed his son Zi as village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan took the throne, he honored Cheng Pu's service and made his son Zi a village marquis.

sentences.zh: 黃蓋字公覆，零陵泉陵人也。

translations.literal: Huang Gai, courtesy name Gongfu, was a man from Quanling in Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gai, styled Gongfu, was from Quanling in Lingling commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：故南陽太守黃子廉之後也，枝葉分離，自祖遷于零陵，遂家焉。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: He was descended from the former Administrator of Nanyang Huang Zilian; branches of the family scattered, and from his grandfather's generation they moved to Lingling and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu traces him to former Nanyang prefect Huang Zilian; the clan scattered, and his grandfather's line moved to Lingling and settled.

sentences.zh: 蓋少孤，嬰丁凶難，辛苦備甞，然有壯志，雖處貧賤，不自同於凡庸，常以負薪餘閑，學書疏，講兵事。〉

translations.literal: Gai was orphaned young and endured bitter hardship, tasting every hardship, yet he had great ambition; though he lived in poverty and low status, he did not rank himself with the common run, and often in the spare time from carrying firewood he studied letters and documents and discussed military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gai lost his parents early and knew every sort of hardship, yet his ambitions ran high; though poor and obscure, he refused to be ordinary, and while gathering firewood he taught himself to read and to study war.

sentences.zh: 初爲郡吏，察孝廉，辟公府。

translations.literal: At first he was a clerk in the commandery, was recommended as filial and incorrupt, and was summoned to the Excellencies' offices.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a county clerk, earned recommendation as filial and incorrupt, and received summons to the capital ministries.

sentences.zh: 孫堅舉義兵，蓋從之。

translations.literal: When Sun Jian raised loyal troops, Gai followed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Jian raised his army, Huang Gai joined him.

sentences.zh: 堅南破山賊，北走董卓，拜蓋別部司馬。

translations.literal: Jian defeated the mountain bandits in the south and drove Dong Zhuo northward in flight, and appointed Gai Major of a Separate Division.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian shattered southern mountain bandits and chased Dong Zhuo north, then named Huang Gai major of a separate division.

sentences.zh: 堅薨，蓋隨策及權，擐甲周旋，蹈刃屠城。

translations.literal: When Jian died, Gai followed Ce and Quan, donned armor and campaigned everywhere, trod blades and stormed cities.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Jian fell, Huang Gai served Ce and Quan in armor through every campaign, storming cities under the blade.

sentences.zh: 諸山越不賔，有寇難之縣，輙用蓋爲守長。

translations.literal: Wherever the Shanyue were not submissive and counties suffered raids, he was repeatedly employed as defending elder.
translations.idiomatic: Where Shanyue defied authority and counties faced raids, they repeatedly named Huang Gai county defender.

sentences.zh: 石城縣吏，特難檢御，蓋乃署兩掾，分主諸曹。

translations.literal: The clerks of Shicheng county were especially hard to control; Gai then appointed two assistants and divided supervision of the various bureaus among them.
translations.idiomatic: Shicheng's clerks were unruly, so Huang Gai appointed two aides and split the bureaus between them.

sentences.zh: 教曰：「令長不德，徒以武功爲官，不以文吏爲稱。

translations.literal: His instruction said: "The magistrate lacks virtue and has gained office only by military merit, not by reputation as a civil clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He announced: "I have little virtue as magistrate—I hold office by martial record, not by civil reputation.

sentences.zh: 今賊寇未平，有軍旅之務，一以文書委付兩掾，當檢攝諸曹，糾擿謬誤。

translations.literal: Now the bandits are not yet pacified and there are military affairs; I wholly entrust the documents to the two assistants; they must oversee the bureaus, inspect and expose errors.
translations.idiomatic: Banditry is not yet ended and camp duties press; I leave all paperwork to these two—they must ride herd on every office and expose mistakes.

sentences.zh: 兩掾所署，事入諾出，若有姦欺，終不加以鞭杖，宜各盡心，無爲衆先。

translations.literal: What the two assistants approve, affairs enter and orders go out; if there is deceit, in the end I will not apply the whip or club—you should each exert your hearts and not take the lead among the multitude in wrongdoing."
translations.idiomatic: What they approve goes through; if anyone cheats, I still will not flog you—but work honestly and do not be first among the crowd to betray the rules."

sentences.zh: 」初皆怖威，夙夜恭職；

translations.literal: At first all feared his authority and diligently attended to duty day and night;
translations.idiomatic: At first they trembled at his sternness and worked day and night;

sentences.zh: 久之，吏以蓋不視文書，漸容人事。

translations.literal: after a long time, the clerks, because Gai did not examine documents, gradually allowed personal favors.
translations.idiomatic: but after a while, seeing he never opened the files, they slowly slipped back to graft.

sentences.zh: 蓋亦嫌外懈怠，時有所省，各得兩掾不奉法數事。

translations.literal: Gai also resented outward laxity; from time to time he inspected and obtained several instances in which the two assistants had not observed the law.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gai grew impatient with their negligence, spot-checked, and caught both assistants breaking the law.

sentences.zh: 乃悉請諸掾吏，賜酒食，因出事詰問。

translations.literal: Then he summoned all the clerks and assistants, feasted them with wine and food, and thereupon produced the matters and questioned them.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned every clerk to a banquet, then confronted them with the evidence.

sentences.zh: 兩掾辭屈，皆叩頭謝罪。

translations.literal: The two assistants were speechless in argument and all knocked their heads and apologized for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The two aides could not reply and kowtowed in guilt.

sentences.zh: 蓋曰：「前已相勑，終不以鞭杖相加，非相欺也。

translations.literal: Gai said: "Earlier I had already admonished you; in the end I would not add whip or club—this was not deceiving you.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gai said: "I warned you that there would be no beatings—that was not an empty promise.

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: " Then he killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Then he executed them.

sentences.zh: 縣中震慄。

translations.literal: The county was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: The whole county went rigid with fear.

sentences.zh: 後轉春穀長，尋陽令。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to be chief of Chungu and magistrate of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on as chief of Chungu and magistrate of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 凡守九縣，所在平定。

translations.literal: In all he defended nine counties; wherever he was, order was established.
translations.idiomatic: He governed nine counties in succession and left each one pacified.

sentences.zh: 遷丹楊都尉，抑彊扶弱，山越懷附。

translations.literal: He was promoted Commandant of Danyang, restrained the strong and aided the weak, and the Shanyue submitted in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: As Danyang commandant he curbed the powerful and shielded the weak until the Shanyue came over willingly.

sentences.zh: 蓋姿貌嚴毅，善於養衆，每所征討，士卒皆爭爲先。

translations.literal: Gai's bearing was stern and firm; he was good at nurturing his troops, and in every campaign the soldiers vied to be first.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and steady, he knew how to keep men loyal—in every campaign his soldiers raced to the front.

sentences.zh: 建安中，隨周瑜拒曹公於赤壁，建策火攻，語在

translations.literal: In the Jian'an period he followed Zhou Yu to resist Cao Cao at Chibi and devised the fire attack; the words are in
translations.idiomatic: Under Jian'an he stood with Zhou Yu at Red Cliffs and devised the fire attack—the account is in

sentences.zh: 〈瑜傳〉。

translations.literal: "Biography of Zhou Yu."
translations.idiomatic: the biography of Zhou Yu.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：赤壁之役，蓋爲流矢所中，時寒墮水，爲吳軍人所得，不知其蓋也，置廁牀中。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: In the Red Cliffs campaign, Gai was struck by a stray arrow; it was cold and he fell into the water, was picked up by Wu soldiers who did not know it was Gai, and was laid on a privy bench.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu says a stray arrow knocked him into the icy water; Wu troops pulled him out without recognizing him and laid him on a latrine bench.

sentences.zh: 蓋自彊以一聲呼韓當，當聞之，曰：「此公覆聲也。

translations.literal: Gai forced himself to call out once to Han Dang; when Dang heard it, he said: "This is Gongfu's voice.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Gai gathered strength and shouted once for Han Dang; Han Dang cried, "That is Gongfu's voice!

sentences.zh: 」向之垂涕，解易其衣，遂以得生。〉

translations.literal: " He went to him weeping, changed his clothes, and thus he survived.
translations.idiomatic: He ran to him weeping, changed his clothes, and Huang Gai lived.

sentences.zh: 拜武鋒中郎將。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Household Who Smashes the Enemy's Front (middle rank).
translations.idiomatic: He was named middle general of the van.

sentences.zh: 武陵蠻夷反亂，攻守城邑，乃以蓋領太守。

translations.literal: The Wuling Man and Yi rebelled and raided, attacking and defending city towns, so Gai was appointed concurrent prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuling tribes rose and besieged towns, Huang Gai was made acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 時郡兵才五百人，自以不敵，因開城門，賊半入，乃擊之，斬首數百，餘皆奔走，盡歸邑落。

translations.literal: At the time the commandery soldiers were only five hundred; thinking himself no match, he opened the city gate; when half the bandits had entered, he struck them, beheading several hundred; the rest all fled and completely returned to their settlements.
translations.idiomatic: With only five hundred men he knew he could not win a stand-up fight, so he opened the gates; when half the raiders were inside he struck, beheading hundreds—the rest fled to their villages.

sentences.zh: 誅討魁帥，附從者赦之。

translations.literal: He executed and attacked the chieftains; those who followed were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He executed the ringleaders and pardoned followers who submitted.

sentences.zh: 自春訖夏，寇亂盡平，諸幽邃巴、醴、由、誕邑侯君長，皆改操易節，奉禮請見，郡境遂清。

translations.literal: From spring through summer the raids were entirely pacified; the peoples of the remote Ba, Li, You, and Dan valleys, every town head and chief, all changed conduct and tokens of allegiance, presented ritual courtesy and asked audience, and the commandery territory was then cleared.
translations.idiomatic: From spring into summer the rebellion ended; headmen of the Ba, Li, You, and Dan peoples in the hidden valleys all switched allegiance, came to court with gifts, and the commandery was quiet.

sentences.zh: 後長沙益陽縣爲山賊所攻，蓋又平討。

translations.literal: Later Yiyang county in Changsha was attacked by mountain bandits, and Gai again pacified them by campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Later when mountain bandits struck Yiyang in Changsha, Huang Gai crushed them again.

sentences.zh: 加偏將軍，病卒于官。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Lieutenant General and died of illness in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to lieutenant general and died in office of illness.

sentences.zh: 蓋當官決斷，事無留滯，國人思之。

translations.literal: Gai was decisive in office; affairs did not linger; the people of the state remembered him.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared official business without backlog, and the realm remembered him.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：又圖畫蓋形，四時祠祭。〉

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: They also painted Gai's likeness and offered seasonal sacrifice in all four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu adds that they painted his portrait and sacrificed to him every season.

sentences.zh: 及權踐阼，追論其功，賜子柄爵關內侯。

translations.literal: When Quan ascended the throne, he posthumously assessed his merit and granted his son Bing noble rank as marquis within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan took the throne, he honored Huang Gai's service and ennobled his son Bing as a marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 韓當字義公，遼西令支人也。

translations.literal: Han Dang, courtesy name Yigong, was a man from Lingzhi in Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Dang, styled Yigong, came from Lingzhi in Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 〈令音郎定反。

translations.literal: (The note: ling is read with the langding fan cutting.
translations.idiomatic: (Phonetic note: "Ling" uses the langding fan cutting.

sentences.zh: 支音巨兒反。〉

translations.literal: zhi is read with the ju'er fan cutting.)
translations.idiomatic: "Zhi" uses the ju'er fan cutting.)

sentences.zh: 以便弓馬，有膂力，幸於孫堅，從征伐周旋，數犯危難，陷敵擒虜，爲別部司馬。

translations.literal: He was skilled with bow and horse, had strength, was favored by Sun Jian, followed on campaigns everywhere, repeatedly braved peril, penetrated the enemy and captured prisoners, and became Major of a Separate Division.
translations.idiomatic: Expert with bow and horse, strong, favored by Sun Jian, he campaigned through danger, broke enemy lines and took prisoners, and rose to major of a separate division.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：當勤苦有功，以軍旅陪隷，分於英豪，故爵位不加。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: Dang toiled with merit, but because he came from the army as a retainer and was distributed among heroes, his noble rank was not advanced.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu says Han Dang earned honors but, raised from the ranks among brilliant peers, never gained matching titles.

sentences.zh: 終於堅世，爲別部司馬。〉

translations.literal: At the end of Jian's era he was Major of a Separate Division.
translations.idiomatic: He ended Sun Jian's lifetime still a major of a separate division.

sentences.zh: 及孫策東渡，從討三郡，遷先登校尉，授兵二千，騎五十匹。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce crossed east, he followed the campaign against three commanderies, was promoted vanguard commandant, and was given two thousand troops and fifty horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce crossed east, Han Dang helped conquer three commanderies, became vanguard commandant, and received two thousand men and fifty horses.

sentences.zh: 從征劉勳，破黃祖，還討鄱陽，領樂安長，山越畏服。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Liu Xun, defeated Huang Zu, returned to campaign against Poyang, served as chief of Le'an, and the Shanyue feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Liu Xun, broke Huang Zu, wheeled to Poyang, governed Le'an as chief, and awed the Shanyue into submission.

sentences.zh: 後以中郎將與周瑜等拒破曹公，又與呂蒙襲取南郡，遷偏將軍，領永昌太守。

translations.literal: Later as middle general together with Zhou Yu and others he resisted and defeated Cao Cao; again with Lü Meng he seized Nan commandery by surprise; he was promoted Lieutenant General and concurrent Prefect of Yongchang.
translations.idiomatic: As middle general he helped Zhou Yu defeat Cao Cao, then with Lü Meng seized Nan commandery by stealth; he rose to lieutenant general and acting Yongchang prefect.

sentences.zh: 宜都之役，與陸遜、朱然等共攻蜀軍於涿鄉，大破之，徙威烈將軍，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: In the Yidu campaign, together with Lu Xun, Zhu Ran, and others he jointly attacked the Shu army at Zhuoxiang and greatly defeated them; he was transferred General Who Inspires Awe, enfeoffed as village marquis of Ducheng.
translations.idiomatic: At Yidu he joined Lu Xun and Zhu Ran to smash the Shu host at Zhuoxiang; he was made awe-inspiring general and village marquis at Ducheng.

sentences.zh: 曹真攻南郡，當保東南。

translations.literal: Cao Zhen attacked Nan commandery; Dang held the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Zhen struck Nan commandery, Han Dang held the southeast sector.

sentences.zh: 在外爲帥，厲將士同心固守，又敬望督司，奉遵法令，權善之。

translations.literal: Outside he was a commander; he encouraged officers and men to stand firm together; he also respected the supervising officials and obeyed laws and orders; Quan approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: In the field he rallied officers and men to a common defense, deferred to supervising officials, and observed regulations—Sun Quan approved.

sentences.zh: 黃武二年，封石城侯，遷昭武將軍，領冠軍太守，後又加都督之號。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangwu he was enfeoffed marquis of Shicheng, promoted General Who Displays Martial Might, concurrently champion prefect, and later the title of area commander was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 2 he became marquis of Shicheng, then shining martial general and champion prefect, with area command added later.

sentences.zh: 將敢死及解煩兵萬人，討丹楊賊，破之。

translations.literal: He led dare-to-die troops and trouble-soother soldiers, ten thousand men, to campaign against Danyang bandits and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He led ten thousand dare-to-die troops and trouble-soother guards against Danyang bandits and broke them.

sentences.zh: 會病卒，子綜襲侯領兵。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness; his son Zong inherited the marquisate and commanded the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died of illness; his son Zong inherited the fief and the command.

sentences.zh: 其年，權征石陽，以綜有憂，使守武昌，而綜淫亂不軌。

translations.literal: That year Quan campaigned at Shiyang; because Zong was in mourning he had him guard Wuchang, but Zong was dissolute and acted contrary to duty.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sun Quan campaigned at Shiyang; because Zong mourned his father he left him to hold Wuchang, but Zong ran wild and broke every rule.

sentences.zh: 權雖以父故不問，綜內懷懼，

translations.literal: Though Quan on account of his father did not question him, Zong inwardly harbored fear,
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan overlooked it for the father's sake, yet Zong lived in dread,

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：綜欲叛，恐左右不從，因諷使劫略，示欲饒之，轉相放效，爲行旅大患。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: Zong wished to rebel but feared those around him would not follow; therefore he incited them to raid and plunder, pretending he would forgive them, and they imitated one another until travelers suffered great harm.
translations.idiomatic: the Book of Wu explains Zong meant to defect but doubted his officers, so he incited them to raid while pretending leniency until banditry scourged the roads.

sentences.zh: 後因詐言被詔，以部曲爲寇盜見詰讓，云「將吏以下，當並收治」，又言恐罪自及。

translations.literal: Later he falsely claimed an imperial edict, was reprimanded for his retainers acting as bandits, saying "from officers downward all shall be arrested together," and again said he feared guilt would reach himself.
translations.idiomatic: He forged word of an edict, then when rebuked for his followers' pillaging claimed that "every rank would be seized together" and that punishment would reach him.

sentences.zh: 左右因曰：「惟當去耳。

translations.literal: Those around him therefore said: "We can only leave."
translations.idiomatic: His men said, "We have to flee."

sentences.zh: 」遂共圖計，以當葬父，盡呼親戚姑姊，悉以嫁將吏，所幸婢妾，皆賜與親近，殺牛飲酒歃血，與共盟誓。〉

translations.literal: " Then they plotted together; borrowing the occasion of burying his father, he summoned all kinswomen and married his sisters out to officers, favored concubines he bestowed on favorites, slaughtered cattle, drank wine, and swore blood with them.
translations.idiomatic: They schemed under cover of his father's funeral: he married sisters to officers, gave concubines to favorites, slaughtered cattle, drank wine, and swore oaths in blood.

sentences.zh: 載父喪，將母家屬部曲男女數千人奔魏。

translations.literal: Loading his father's coffin, he took his mother, household, and retainers, men and women several thousand, and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He loaded the coffin and led his mother, household, and thousands of retainers across to Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏以爲將軍，封廣陽侯。

translations.literal: Wei made him a general and enfeoffed him marquis of Guangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wei named him a general and marquis of Guangyang.

sentences.zh: 數犯邊境，殺害人民，權常切齒。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he violated the border and killed the people; Quan constantly gnashed his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: He raided the frontier again and again; Sun Quan ground his teeth at the name.

sentences.zh: 東興之役，綜爲前鋒，軍敗身死，諸葛恪斬送其首，以白權廟。

translations.literal: In the Dongxing campaign Zong was vanguard; the army was defeated and he died; Zhuge Ke sent his head to display before Quan's temple.
translations.idiomatic: At Dongxing he led the van, died when the army broke, and Zhuge Ke sent his head to Sun Quan's shrine.

sentences.zh: 蔣欽字公弈，九江壽春人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Qin, courtesy name Gongyi, was a man from Shouchun in Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qin, styled Gongyi, was from Shouchun in Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 孫策之襲袁術，欽隨從給事。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce struck Yuan Shu, Qin followed and served as attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce moved against Yuan Shu, Jiang Qin followed as an aide.

sentences.zh: 及策東渡，拜別部司馬，授兵。

translations.literal: When Ce crossed east, he was appointed Major of a Separate Division and given troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Ce crossed east, Jiang Qin became major of a separate division with a command.

sentences.zh: 與策周旋，平定三郡，又從定豫章。

translations.literal: He campaigned with Ce, pacified three commanderies, and again followed the settlement of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He helped Ce secure three commanderies, then helped take Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 調授葛陽尉，歷三縣長，討平盜賊，遷西部都尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed magistrate of Geyang, served as chief of three counties, campaigned against and pacified bandits, and was promoted western commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Geyang magistrate, he headed three counties, cleared bandits, and rose to western commandant.

sentences.zh: 會稽冶賊呂合、秦狼等爲亂，欽將兵討擊，遂禽合、狼，五縣平定，徙討越中郎將，以涇拘、昭陽爲奉邑。

translations.literal: The metallurgical bandits of Kuaiji, Lü He and Qin Lang, and others made rebellion; Qin led troops to strike them and captured He and Lang; five counties were pacified; he was transferred General Who Campaigns Against the Yue (middle rank), with Jingju and Zhaoyang as benefice holdings.
translations.idiomatic: Kuaiji furnace rebels Lü He and Qin Lang rose; Jiang Qin captured both, quieted five counties, became middle general who campaigns against the Yue, with Jingju and Zhaoyang as benefices.

sentences.zh: 賀齊討黝賊，欽督萬兵，與齊并力，黝賊平定。

translations.literal: He Qi campaigned against the You bandits; Qin commanded ten thousand troops and joined forces with Qi; the You bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When He Qi attacked You bandits, Jiang Qin brought ten thousand men and helped crush them.

sentences.zh: 從征合肥，魏將張遼襲權於津北，欽力戰有功，遷盪寇將軍，領濡須督。

translations.literal: He followed the expedition to Hefei; Wei general Zhang Liao raided Quan north of the ford; Qin fought hard and had merit; he was promoted General Who Sweeps Away the Bandits and superintendent of Ruxu.
translations.idiomatic: At Hefei, when Zhang Liao ambushed Sun Quan north of the crossing, Jiang Qin fought fiercely, earned promotion to general who sweeps bandits, and took charge of Ruxu.

sentences.zh: 後召還都，拜津右護軍，典領辭訟。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned back to the capital and appointed protector of the army on the right of the ford, in charge of lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he became right protector at the crossing and heard litigation.

sentences.zh: 權甞入其堂內，母踈帳縹被，妻妾布裙。

translations.literal: Quan once entered his hall; his mother had thin curtains and a pale coverlet, his wives and concubines cotton skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan once entered his home: his mother had thin curtains and a plain quilt; wives and concubines wore cotton skirts.

sentences.zh: 權歎其在貴守約，即勑御府爲母作錦被，改易帷帳，妻妾衣服悉皆錦繡。

translations.literal: Quan sighed that though noble he kept austerity; he immediately ordered the imperial wardrobe to make a brocade coverlet for his mother and change the curtains and hangings; the wives' and concubines' clothing was all brocade embroidery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan marveled at such austerity in a high minister and ordered the palace tailors to brocade his mother's bed, replace the hangings, and dress every wife and concubine in embroidery.

sentences.zh: 初，欽屯宣城，甞討豫章賊。

translations.literal: At first Qin was stationed at Xuancheng; he once campaigned against bandits in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qin had been garrisoned at Xuancheng and once cleared Yuzhang bandits.

sentences.zh: 蕪湖令徐盛收欽屯吏，表斬之，權以欽在遠不許，盛由是自嫌於欽。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Wuhu, Xu Sheng, arrested Qin's garrison clerk and memorialized to execute him; Quan, because Qin was far away, did not permit it; Sheng therefore personally bore ill will toward Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Wuhu magistrate Xu Sheng jailed one of Jiang Qin's clerks and sought execution; Sun Quan, with Jiang Qin away, refused—so Xu Sheng nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 曹公出濡須，欽與呂蒙持諸軍節度。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao came out to Ruxu, Qin with Lü Meng held joint command of all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao advanced on Ruxu, Jiang Qin and Lü Meng directed every corps.

sentences.zh: 盛常畏欽因事害己，而欽每稱其善。

translations.literal: Sheng always feared Qin would harm him on some pretext, but Qin always praised his good qualities.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sheng feared Jiang Qin would use any excuse against him, yet Jiang Qin kept praising him.

sentences.zh: 盛旣服德，論者美焉。

translations.literal: Sheng had already submitted to his virtue; commentators praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xu Sheng yielded to Jiang Qin's magnanimity, observers praised the deed.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：權謂欽曰：「盛前白卿，卿今舉盛，欲慕祁奚邪？

translations.literal: 《Accounts from Beyond the Yangzi》 says: Quan said to Qin: "Sheng earlier denounced you to me; you now recommend Sheng—do you mean to imitate Qi Xi?"
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan records Sun Quan telling Jiang Qin, "Xu Sheng once spoke against you; now you praise him—are you playing Qi Xi?"

sentences.zh: 」欽對曰：「臣聞公舉不挾私怨，盛忠而勤彊，有膽略器用，好萬人督也。

translations.literal: " Qin replied: "I have heard that fair recommendation does not carry private grudges; Sheng is loyal, diligent, and strong, has courage, strategy, and practical talent, and is fit to command ten thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Qin answered, "A principled nomination holds no spite. Xu Sheng is loyal, tireless, brave, and resourceful—the right man to lead ten thousand men."

sentences.zh: 今大事未定，臣當助國求才，豈敢挾私恨以蔽賢乎！

translations.literal: Now the great enterprise is not yet settled; I ought to help the state seek men of talent—how dare I let private hatred hide the worthy!"
translations.idiomatic: With the realm still unsettled, I must help you find able men. How could I let old resentments block a worthy officer?"

sentences.zh: 」權嘉之。〉

translations.literal: " Quan commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan approved.

sentences.zh: 權討關羽，欽督水軍入沔，還，道病卒。

translations.literal: When Quan campaigned against Guan Yu, Qin commanded the water forces into the Han; on the return he died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Guan Yu, Jiang Qin led the fleet up the Han; he died of sickness on the march home.

sentences.zh: 權素服舉哀，以蕪湖民二百戶、田二百頃，給欽妻子。

translations.literal: Quan wore mourning dress and observed lamentation, and granted Qin's wife and children two hundred Wuhu households and two hundred qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wore white and mourned him, endowing his family with two hundred Wuhu households and two hundred qing of land.

sentences.zh: 子壹封宣城侯，領兵拒劉備有功，還赴南郡，與魏交戰，臨陣卒。

translations.literal: His son Yi was enfeoffed marquis of Xuancheng; leading troops he resisted Liu Bei with merit, returned to answer the summons to Nan commandery, fought Wei, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi became marquis of Xuancheng, distinguished himself against Liu Bei, rushed to Nan commandery to fight Wei, and fell in combat.

sentences.zh: 壹無子，弟休領兵，後有罪失業。

translations.literal: Yi had no son; younger brother Xiu commanded the troops; later he committed a crime and lost his position.
translations.idiomatic: Yi left no heir; his brother Xiu took the command until crime stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 周泰字幼平，九江下蔡人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Tai, courtesy name Youping, was a man of Xiachai in Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tai, styled Youping, hailed from Xiachai in Jiujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 與蔣欽隨孫策爲左右，服事恭敬，數戰有功。

translations.literal: Together with Jiang Qin he followed Sun Ce as attendants to his left and right; he served respectfully and repeatedly fought with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jiang Qin attended Sun Ce as body companions—dutiful in service and decorated in battle.

sentences.zh: 策入會稽，署別部司馬，授兵。

translations.literal: When Ce entered Kuaiji, he appointed him Major of a Separate Division and gave him troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ce took Kuaiji, Zhou Tai became major of a separate division with a command.

sentences.zh: 權愛其爲人，請以自給。

translations.literal: Quan loved his character and asked to have him attend on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan admired him and asked Ce to assign him to his own household guard.

sentences.zh: 策討六縣山賊，權住宣城，使士自衞，不能千人，意尚忽略，不治圍落，而山賊數千人卒至。

translations.literal: Ce campaigned against the mountain bandits of six counties; Quan stayed at Xuancheng and had soldiers guard him—not reaching a thousand men—and his mind was still heedless; he did not build palisades, and several thousand mountain bandits suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: While Ce cleared six counties of bandits, Sun Quan stayed at Xuancheng with fewer than a thousand guards, careless of defenses; thousands of highlanders suddenly surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 權始得上馬，而賊鋒刃已交於左右，或斫中馬鞌，衆莫能自定。

translations.literal: Quan had just mounted when the bandits' blades were already crossing on his left and right; some struck the saddle; the crowd could not steady themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely reached the saddle when steel flashed on both sides—one blow split the skirt—and his men panicked.

sentences.zh: 惟泰奮激，投身衞權，膽氣倍人，左右由泰並能就戰。

translations.literal: Only Tai roused himself and threw his body to shield Quan; his courage doubled that of others; those around him through Tai could all join battle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tai alone threw himself in front of Sun Quan with redoubled courage, rallying everyone near him to fight.

sentences.zh: 賊旣解散，身被十二創，良乆乃蘇。

translations.literal: When the bandits had scattered, his body bore twelve wounds; only after a long time did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders broke off, twelve wounds marked his body; long moments passed before he stirred.

sentences.zh: 是日無泰，權幾危殆。

translations.literal: That day without Tai, Quan would nearly have perished.
translations.idiomatic: Without Zhou Tai that day, Sun Quan would almost have been lost.

sentences.zh: 策深德之，補春穀長。

translations.literal: Ce deeply valued him and appointed him chief of Chungu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce honored him with appointment as chief of Chungu county.

sentences.zh: 後從攻皖，及討江夏，還過豫章，復補宜春長，所在皆食其征賦。

translations.literal: Later he followed the attack on Wan and the campaign against Jiangxia; on the return passing through Yuzhang he was again appointed chief of Yichun; everywhere they drew support from local taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Wan and Jiangxia, then passing Yuzhang was named chief of Yichun; each post supplied his revenue from its assessments.

sentences.zh: 從討黃祖有功。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Huang Zu with merit.
translations.idiomatic: He earned credit in the campaign against Huang Zu.

sentences.zh: 後與周瑜、程普拒曹公於赤壁，攻曹仁於南郡。

translations.literal: Later with Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu he resisted Cao Cao at Chibi and attacked Cao Ren in Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he stood with Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu at Red Cliffs and besieged Cao Ren in Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 荊州平定，將兵屯岑。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou was pacified, he led troops and garrisoned Cen.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingzhou submitted, he encamped at Cen with his division.

sentences.zh: 曹公出濡須，泰復赴擊，曹公退，留督濡須，拜平虜將軍。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao came out to Ruxu, Tai again went to strike; Cao Cao withdrew; Tai was left to supervise Ruxu and was appointed General Who Pacifies the Caitiffs.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao advanced on Ruxu, Zhou Tai counterattacked and forced his retreat, then stayed on as Ruxu superintendent and general who pacifies captives.

sentences.zh: 時朱然、徐盛等皆在所部，並不伏也，權特爲案行至濡須鄔，因會諸將，大爲酣樂。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Ran, Xu Sheng, and others were all under his command and would not submit [to his authority]; Quan specially went on inspection to Ruxu Wu, thereupon assembled the generals, and made great merry drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ran, Xu Sheng, and others under his command still bridled at his rank, so Sun Quan traveled to Ruxu Wu, gathered the officers, and held a lavish banquet.

sentences.zh: 權自行酒到泰前，命泰解衣，權手自指其創痕，問以所起。

translations.literal: Quan personally carried wine to Tai's seat, ordered Tai to remove his clothes, and with his own hand pointed to the scar marks, asking when each arose.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan poured wine at Zhou Tai's place himself, told him to strip, and traced each scar, asking which battle had left it.

sentences.zh: 泰輒記昔戰鬬處以對，畢，使復服，歡讌極夜。

translations.literal: Tai then recalled the former battles and answered; when finished, he was made to dress again, and they feasted merrily until the night was spent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Tai named each fight in turn; when he was clothed again they feasted far into the night.

sentences.zh: 其明日，遣使者授以御蓋。

translations.literal: The next day he sent an envoy to grant him the imperial umbrella-canopy.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning an envoy presented him with the imperial parasol.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：權把其臂，因流涕交連，字之曰：「幼平，卿爲孤兄弟戰如熊虎，不惜軀命，被創數十，膚如刻畫，孤亦何心不待卿以骨肉之恩，委卿以兵馬之重乎！

translations.literal: 《Accounts from Beyond the Yangzi》 says: Quan grasped his arm, and tears streamed mingling; he addressed him by style: "Youping, you have fought for my brothers like bears and tigers, sparing not your body; you have suffered dozens of wounds, your skin like carved lines—what heart could I have not to treat you with the kindness of flesh and bone and entrust you with the weight of troops and horses!
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan adds that Sun Quan seized his arm, weeping: "Youping, you fight for my kin like tiger or bear—you gave your body dozens of scars etched like ink—how could I withhold the trust of kinship or the burden of command?"

sentences.zh: 卿吳之功臣，孤當與卿同榮辱，等休戚。

translations.literal: You are Wu's meritorious minister; I ought to share glory and shame with you, equal in joy and sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: You are a pillar of Wu; I will share honor and disaster with you alike."

sentences.zh: 幼平意快爲之，勿以寒門自退也。

translations.literal: Youping, act as your heart freely chooses; do not withdraw yourself because of humble origins."
translations.idiomatic: Take heart from your deeds and never shrink back for humble birth."

sentences.zh: 」即勑以己常所用御幘青縑蓋賜之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered that his own usual imperial turban and pale-blue gauze canopy be granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Zhou Tai his own imperial headcloth and blue silk canopy.

sentences.zh: 坐罷，住駕，使泰以兵馬導從出，鳴鼓角作鼓吹。〉

translations.literal: When the sitting ended, halting the carriage, he had Tai escort out with troops and horses as escort, sounding drums and horns as martial music.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet broke up he halted his carriage and had Zhou Tai ride escort with drums, horns, and pipes sounding.

sentences.zh: 於是盛等乃伏。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sheng and others then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Xu Sheng and the rest yield their resentment.

sentences.zh: 後權破關羽，欲進圖蜀，拜泰漢中太守、奮威將軍，封陵陽侯。

translations.literal: Later when Quan defeated Guan Yu and wished to advance to plan against Shu, he appointed Tai Prefect of Hanzhong and General Who Displays Might, enfeoffed him marquis of Lingyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan broke Guan Yu and turned toward Shu, he named Zhou Tai prefect of Hanzhong and awe-inspiring general, marquis of Lingyang.

sentences.zh: 黃武中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Huangwu era.
translations.idiomatic: He died sometime in the Huangwu reign.

sentences.zh: 子邵以騎都尉領兵。

translations.literal: His son Shao as Cavalry Commandant commanded troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao led troops as cavalry commandant.

sentences.zh: 曹仁出濡須，戰有功，又從攻破曹休，進位裨將軍，黃龍二年卒。

translations.literal: When Cao Ren came out to Ruxu he fought with merit; again he followed the defeat of Cao Xiu and advanced to Major General; he died in the second year of Huanglong.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself against Cao Ren at Ruxu, helped crush Cao Xiu, rose to major general, and died in Huanglong 2.

sentences.zh: 弟承領兵襲侯。

translations.literal: Younger brother Cheng commanded troops and inherited the marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Cheng inherited the fief and the command.

sentences.zh: 陳武字子烈，廬江松滋人。

translations.literal: Chen Wu, courtesy name Zilie, was a man of Songzi in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu, styled Zilie, came from Songzi in Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 孫策在壽春，武往脩謁，時年十八，長七尺七寸，因從渡江，征討有功，拜別部司馬。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce was at Shouchun, Wu went to pay formal visit; he was then eighteen sui, seven chi seven cun tall; he therefore followed across the river and campaigned with merit, appointed Major of a Separate Division.
translations.idiomatic: He introduced himself to Sun Ce at Shouchun at eighteen, stood seven chi seven cun, crossed the Yangzi with him, won honors in the field, and became major of a separate division.

sentences.zh: 策破劉勳，多得廬江人，料其精銳，乃以武爲督，所向無前。

translations.literal: Ce defeated Liu Xun and obtained many men of Lujiang; selecting their crack troops, he made Wu commander; wherever he turned none stood before him.
translations.idiomatic: After Ce shattered Liu Xun he drafted Lujiang's best fighters under Chen Wu, who led them unstoppable against every foe.

sentences.zh: 及權統事，轉督五校。

translations.literal: When Quan took charge of affairs, he was transferred to command the Five Camps.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan took power, Chen Wu was shifted to command the Five Camps.

sentences.zh: 仁厚好施，鄉里遠方客多依託之。

translations.literal: Kind and generous, fond of giving, many from the countryside and distant guests relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Warm and open-handed, he sheltered neighbors and wanderers alike.

sentences.zh: 尤爲權所親愛，數至其家。

translations.literal: Quan especially loved him and repeatedly went to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan favored him above most and often visited his house.

sentences.zh: 累有功勞，進位偏將軍。

translations.literal: Accumulating merit, he advanced to Lieutenant General.
translations.idiomatic: Merit carried him to lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 建安二十年，從擊合肥，奮命戰死。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jian'an he followed the strike on Hefei and died fighting, staking his life.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 20 he stormed Hefei and died charging the line.

sentences.zh: 權哀之，自臨其葬。

translations.literal: Quan mourned him and personally attended his burial.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan grieved and walked in his funeral cortège.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：權命以其愛妾殉葬，復客二百家。

translations.literal: 《Accounts from Beyond the Yangzi》 says: Quan ordered his beloved concubine to be buried with him, and also two hundred client households.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan says Sun Quan buried a favorite concubine with him and settled two hundred client households on the clan.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：昔三良從秦穆師以之不征；

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: Formerly the Three Worthies followed Duke Mu of Qin to the grave; for that reason his hosts marched no more;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng judged: When the Three Good ministers followed Duke Mu of Qin into death, Qin gained no further campaigns from it;

sentences.zh: 魏妾旣出，杜回以之僵仆。

translations.literal: When Wei Ji's daughter came forth [as ghost], Du Hui thereby fell prostrate.
translations.idiomatic: when Wei Ji's daughter intervened, Du Hui toppled dead on the field.

sentences.zh: 禍福之報，如此之效也。

translations.literal: The retribution of fortune and misfortune has effects like these.
translations.idiomatic: Blessing and curse repay deeds in just this way.

sentences.zh: 權仗計任術，以生從死，世祚之促，不亦宜乎！〉

translations.literal: Quan relied on schemes and employed stratagems, using the living to follow the dead—was it not fitting that his dynasty's fortune should be brief!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan trafficked in plots and sent the living to serve the dead—small wonder his line's fortune proved short."

sentences.zh: 子脩有武風，年十九，權召見獎厲，拜別部司馬，授兵五百人。

translations.literal: His son Xiu had Wu's martial bearing; at nineteen Quan summoned him, praised and encouraged him, appointed Major of a Separate Division, and gave five hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiu inherited his soldierly dash; at nineteen Sun Quan received him, praised him, and gave him five hundred men as major of a separate division.

sentences.zh: 時諸新兵多有逃叛，而脩撫循得意，不失一人。

translations.literal: At the time many of the new troops fled or rebelled, but Xiu soothed and guided them successfully and lost not a single man.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh levies were deserting everywhere, yet Xiu steadied his draft so thoroughly that none slipped away.

sentences.zh: 權奇之，拜爲校尉。

translations.literal: Quan marveled at him and appointed him Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan took notice and named him commandant.

sentences.zh: 建安末，追錄功臣後，封脩都亭侯，爲解煩督。

translations.literal: At the end of Jian'an, posthumously registering the descendants of meritorious ministers, he enfeoffed Xiu as village marquis of Ducheng and made him commander of the trouble-soother troops.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jian'an, when merit-clans were rewarded, Xiu became village marquis at the metropolitan lodge and commander of the trouble-soother guard.

sentences.zh: 黃龍元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Huanglong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Huanglong 1.

sentences.zh: 庶子 陳表

translations.literal: Son by a concubine: Chen Biao
translations.idiomatic: Chen Biao, the son born to a concubine.

sentences.zh: 弟表，字文奧，武庶子也，少知名，與諸葛恪、顧譚、張休等並侍東宮，皆共親友。

translations.literal: Younger brother Biao, courtesy name Wen'ao, was Wu's son by a concubine; he was known young; together with Zhuge Ke, Gu Tan, Zhang Xiu, and others he attended the Eastern Palace, all close friends.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Biao, styled Wen'ao, was Chen Wu's younger son by a concubine—known early, and joined Zhuge Ke, Gu Tan, and Zhang Xiu as companions in the heir's palace.

sentences.zh: 尚書曁豔亦與表善，後豔遇罪，時人咸自營護，信厚言薄，表獨不然，士以此重之。

translations.literal: Director Ji Yan was also friendly with Biao; later Yan encountered guilt; people of the time all sought to protect themselves—faith thick words thin—but Biao alone was not so; gentlemen therefore esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Director Ji Yan was another friend; when Yan fell afoul of the law everyone rushed to distance themselves, yet Biao stood by him—scholars admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 徙太子中庶子，拜翼正都尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace attendant to the heir apparent and appointed Colonel Who Supports Rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to palace attendant to the heir and colonel who supports rectitude.

sentences.zh: 兄脩亡後，表母不肯事脩母，表謂其母曰：「兄不幸早亡，表統家事，當奉嫡母。

translations.literal: After elder brother Xiu died, Biao's mother was unwilling to serve Xiu's mother; Biao said to his mother: "Elder brother unfortunately died early; Biao manages the household affairs and ought to honor the principal mother.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu died, Biao's birth mother refused to serve Xiu's widowed mother; Biao told her, "My brother died young; I head this household and must honor our lawful mother.

sentences.zh: 母若能爲表屈情，承順嫡母者，是至願也；

translations.literal: If Mother can for Biao bend your feelings and obey the principal mother, that is my utmost wish;
translations.idiomatic: If you can humble yourself and obey her, nothing would please me more;

sentences.zh: 若母不能，直當出別居耳。

translations.literal: if Mother cannot, I must simply leave and live apart."
translations.idiomatic: if not, I will move out and live apart."

sentences.zh: 」表於大義公正如此。

translations.literal: Biao in great righteousness was thus upright.
translations.idiomatic: Such was Chen Biao's sense of duty.

sentences.zh: 由是二母感寤雍穆。

translations.literal: Thereby the two mothers were moved to insight and lived in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Both women were moved and learned to live at peace.

sentences.zh: 表以父死敵場，求用爲將，領兵五百人。

translations.literal: Biao because his father died on the enemy field requested appointment as general and commanded five hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father fell on campaign, Chen Biao asked for a general's commission and five hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 表欲得戰士之力，傾意接待，士皆愛附，樂爲用命。

translations.literal: Biao wished to obtain the strength of fighting men; he poured his heart into receiving them; the soldiers all loved and attached themselves, gladly dying on command.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to winning stalwarts—men loved him and would die at his word.

sentences.zh: 時有盜官物者，疑無難士施明。

translations.literal: At the time someone stole government goods; suspicion fell on the trouble-free soldier Shi Ming.
translations.idiomatic: When government stores were stolen, blame settled on the elite guardsman Shi Ming.

sentences.zh: 明素壯悍，收考極毒，惟死無辭，廷尉以聞。

translations.literal: Ming was by nature fierce; under arrest and torture extremely cruel, only death—no confession; the Commandant of Justice reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Ming was stubborn and fierce; torture could wring no confession short of death, so the Commandant of Justice reported upward.

sentences.zh: 權以表能得健兒之心，詔以明付表，使自以意求其情實。

translations.literal: Quan because Biao could win the hearts of stalwarts, ordered Ming handed to Biao and had him seek the real circumstances as he thought fit.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan, trusting Chen Biao with fighting men, handed Shi Ming to him to extract the truth his own way.

sentences.zh: 表便破械沐浴，易其衣服，厚設酒食，歡以誘之。

translations.literal: Biao then broke his fetters, bathed him, changed his clothes, lavishly set out wine and food, and with kindness enticed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Biao struck off the shackles, bathed and reclothed him, feasted him generously, and drew him out with kindness.

sentences.zh: 明乃首服，具列支黨。

translations.literal: Ming then confessed and fully listed the accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ming confessed and named every accomplice.

sentences.zh: 表以狀聞。

translations.literal: Biao reported the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Biao forwarded the entire confession.

sentences.zh: 權奇之，欲全其名，特爲赦明，誅戮其黨。

translations.literal: Quan marveled and wished to preserve his reputation; specially pardoned Ming and executed his gang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan admired the handling, spared Shi Ming to preserve his honor, and executed the ring instead.

sentences.zh: 遷表爲無難右部督，封都亭侯，以繼舊爵。

translations.literal: Biao was promoted commander of the right division of the trouble-free guard, enfeoffed village marquis of Ducheng, to succeed the old noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Biao rose to command the right wing of the elite guard and inherited the village marquisate.

sentences.zh: 表皆陳讓，乞以傳脩子延，權不許。

translations.literal: Biao both times declined and begged to pass [the fief] to Xiu's son Yan; Quan did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: He declined repeatedly, asking to pass the title to Xiu's son Yan; Sun Quan refused.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾三年，諸葛恪領丹楊太守，討平山越，以表領新安都尉，與恪參勢。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiahe, Zhuge Ke held concurrent Prefect of Danyang, campaigned and pacified the Shanyue; Biao was appointed concurrent Commandant of Xin'an and shared authority with Ke.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiahe 3 Zhuge Ke as Danyang prefect crushed the Shanyue; Chen Biao served as Xin'an commandant beside him.

sentences.zh: 初，表所受賜復人得二百家，在會稽新安縣。

translations.literal: At first, the tax-exempt households Biao had been granted numbered two hundred families, in Xin'an county of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred tax-exempt households in Kuaiji's Xin'an county had been granted him at first.

sentences.zh: 表簡視其人，皆堪好兵，乃上疏陳讓，乞以還官，充足精銳。

translations.literal: Biao reviewed these people; all were fit for good soldiers; he therefore memorialized declining and begged to return them to the state to fill out crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting them he found every man fit for service, memorialized to return them to the rolls, and asked to draft them as crack troops.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「先將軍有功於國，國家以此報之，卿何得辭焉？

translations.literal: An edict said: "The late general had merit for the state; the state rewards thus—how can you decline?"
translations.idiomatic: The court replied: "Your father earned these households; the throne pays its debt—why refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」表乃稱曰：「今除國賊，報父之仇，以人爲本。

translations.literal: Biao then stated: "Now to eliminate the state's enemy and avenge my father's death, men are the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Biao answered: "To destroy our foe and avenge my father I need soldiers, not servants.

sentences.zh: 空枉此勁銳以爲僮僕，非表志也。

translations.literal: To vainly waste these stalwart men as servants and slaves is not Biao's intent."
translations.idiomatic: To squander such fighters as household slaves is not my aim."

sentences.zh: 」皆輒料取以充部伍。

translations.literal: He then selected them all to fill his units.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted them wholesale into his command.

sentences.zh: 所在以聞，權甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The places reported upward; Quan greatly approved.
translations.idiomatic: County officials relayed the story; Sun Quan praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 下郡縣，料正戶羸民以補其處。

translations.literal: He ordered commanderies and counties to assess proper households and weak people to replace those places.
translations.idiomatic: He told counties to shift ordinary households into the vacated settlements.

sentences.zh: 表在官三年，廣開降納，得兵萬餘人。

translations.literal: Biao in office three years widely opened surrender and acceptance and obtained more than ten thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In three years of office he recruited widely and raised ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 事捷當出，會鄱陽民吳遽等爲亂，攻沒城郭，屬縣搖動，表便越界赴討，遽以破敗，遂降。

translations.literal: When the affair was won he ought to have gone out; it happened that Poyang commoners Wu Ju and others rebelled, attacked and took cities; dependent counties were shaken; Biao then crossed boundaries to campaign against them; Ju was defeated and broke, then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ready to march out on success, he learned that Wu Ju of Poyang had seized towns and shaken the district; Chen Biao crossed lines to strike, shattered Wu Ju, and accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 陸遜拜表偏將軍，進封都鄉侯，北屯章阬。

translations.literal: Lu Xun appointed Biao Lieutenant General and advanced his enfeoffment to metropolitan village marquis; he stationed north at Zhangkeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun named him lieutenant general, raised his fief to metropolitan village marquis, and posted him north at Zhangkeng.

sentences.zh: 年三十四卒。

translations.literal: He died at thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-four sui.

sentences.zh: 家財盡於養士，死之日，妻子露立，太子登爲起屋宅。

translations.literal: His household wealth was exhausted in nurturing men of purpose; on the day he died his wife and children stood exposed [without shelter]; the heir Deng built them a house.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his fortune supporting fighting men; when he died his family stood homeless until Crown Prince Deng built them a house.

sentences.zh: 子敖年十七，拜別部司馬，授兵四百人。

translations.literal: His son Ao at seventeen was appointed Major of a Separate Division and given four hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ao became major of a separate division at seventeen with four hundred soldiers.

sentences.zh: 敖卒，脩子延復爲司馬代敖。

translations.literal: When Ao died, Xiu's son Yan again became major in Ao's place.
translations.idiomatic: When Ao died, Xiu's son Yan replaced him as major.

sentences.zh: 延弟永，將軍，封侯。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Yong was a general and enfeoffed marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's brother Yong reached general's rank with a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 始施明感表，自變行爲善，遂成健將，致位將軍。

translations.literal: From the beginning Shi Ming was moved by Biao, changed his conduct to goodness, and thus became a stalwart commander, reaching the rank of general.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Ming, grateful to Chen Biao, reformed and rose from soldier to general.

sentences.zh: 董襲字元代，會稽餘姚人，長八尺，武力過人。

translations.literal: Dong Xi, courtesy name Yuandai, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji, eight chi tall, martial strength surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xi, styled Yuandai, was from Yuyao in Kuaiji—eight chi tall and stronger than ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 〈謝承《後漢書》稱襲志節慷慨，武毅猛烈。〉

translations.literal: Xie Cheng's 《Book of Later Han》 says Xi had lofty integrity and generous spirit, martial vigor and fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Cheng's Hou Hanshu praises his heroic temper and fierce valor.

sentences.zh: 孫策入郡，襲迎於高遷亭，策見而偉之，到署門下賊曹。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce entered the commandery, Xi welcomed him at Gaoxian Pavilion; Ce saw him and thought him impressive; on arrival he appointed him Bandit Bureau under the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce met Dong Xi at Gaoxian pavilion, admired him at sight, and named him bandit-section clerk at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 時山陰宿賊黃龍羅、周勃聚黨數千人，策自出討，襲身斬羅、勃首，還拜別部司馬，授兵數千，遷揚武都尉。

translations.literal: At the time the entrenched bandits of Shanyin, Huang Longluo and Zhou Bo, gathered a faction of several thousand; Ce personally went out to campaign; Xi personally beheaded Luo and Bo; on return he was appointed Major of a Separate Division, given several thousand troops, and promoted Metropolitan Commandant Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: When thousand-strong gangs led by Huang Longluo and Zhou Bo plagued Shanyin, Ce led in person; Dong Xi took both chiefs' heads, earned major of a separate division, thousands of men, and promotion to metropolitan commandant who displays martial might.

sentences.zh: 從策攻皖，又討劉勳於尋陽，伐黃祖於江夏。

translations.literal: He followed Ce's attack on Wan, also campaigned against Liu Xun at Xunyang, and struck Huang Zu in Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Sun Ce at Wan and Xunyang and fought Huang Zu in Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 策薨，權年少，初統事，太妃憂之，引見張昭及襲等，問江東可保安不，襲對曰：「江東地勢有山川之固，而討逆明府恩德在民。

translations.literal: When Ce died, Quan was young and had just taken charge; the Grand Imperial Concubine worried, summoned Zhang Zhao and Xi and others, and asked whether the lands east of the Yangzi could be kept secure; Xi replied: "The terrain of Jiangdong has the firmness of mountains and rivers, and the grace of the General Who Attacks Rebels rests with the people.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Ce died, young Sun Quan took power and his mother feared for him; she called in Zhang Zhao and Dong Xi and asked whether Wu could hold the east. Dong Xi answered: "The rivers and hills defend you, and the late General Who Attacks Rebels won the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 討虜承基，大小用命，張昭秉衆事，襲等爲爪牙，此地利人和之時也，萬無所憂。

translations.literal: The General Who Attacks the Caitiffs inherits the foundation; great and small obey orders; Zhang Zhao manages affairs; Xi and others are claws and fangs—this is the hour of terrain and harmony; there is utterly nothing to fear."
translations.idiomatic: Your brother's heir carries on the task; everyone answers to your command; Zhang Zhao runs civil business and we are your teeth and claws—fortune and terrain favor you. You need not worry."

sentences.zh: 」衆皆壯其言。

translations.literal: The crowd all found his words stirring.
translations.idiomatic: Those present took courage from his words.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽賊彭虎等衆數萬人，襲與凌統、步隲、蔣欽各別分討。

translations.literal: The Poyang bandit Peng Hu and others had a host of tens of thousands; Xi with Ling Tong, Bu Zhi, and Jiang Qin each led a separate column against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Peng Hu of Poyang raised tens of thousands, Dong Xi split forces with Ling Tong, Bu Zhi, and Jiang Qin to strike each wing.

sentences.zh: 襲所向輒破，虎等望見旌旗，便散走，旬日盡平，拜威越校尉，遷偏將軍。

translations.literal: Wherever Xi went he shattered them; Hu and others, seeing the banners, scattered and fled; within ten days all was pacified; he was appointed Colonel Who Surpasses Might and promoted Lieutenant General.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xi swept his sector—Peng Hu's men fled at sight of his standards—and inside ten days the rising was over; he became colonel who surpasses might and lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 建安十三年，權討黃祖。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jian'an, Quan campaigned against Huang Zu.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 13 Sun Quan marched against Huang Zu.

sentences.zh: 祖橫兩蒙衝挾守沔口，以栟閭大紲繫石爲矴，上有千人，以弩交射，飛矢雨下，軍不得前。

translations.literal: Zu stretched two covered swoopers across to guard the Han mouth, bound giant hawthorn hawser cables to stones as anchors; a thousand men above shot crossbows at one another, arrows fell like rain, and the army could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu chained two tower ships across the Han estuary with hawser cables weighted by stones; a thousand bowmen aloft filled the sky with bolts until Wu could not close.

sentences.zh: 襲與凌統俱爲前部，各將敢死百人，人被兩鎧，乘大舸船，突入蒙衝裏。

translations.literal: Xi and Ling Tong both served as vanguard; each led a hundred dare-to-die soldiers wearing double armor aboard large barges and burst inside the covered swoopers.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xi and Ling Tong led the van with picked men in double mail aboard heavy barges and drove into the chained ships.

sentences.zh: 襲身以刀斷兩紲，蒙衝乃橫流，大兵遂進。

translations.literal: Xi personally cut the two cables with a knife; the covered swoopers then drifted cross-current, and the main host advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xi himself severed both cables; the barricade ships spun loose in the current and the fleet pushed through.

sentences.zh: 祖便開門走，兵追斬之。

translations.literal: Zu then opened the gate and fled; pursuing troops struck him down and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu bolted from the gate; pursuit overtook him and took his head.

sentences.zh: 明日大會，權舉觴屬襲曰：「今日之會，斷紲之功也。」

translations.literal: The next day at the great assembly Quan raised a cup toward Xi and said: "This gathering today is owed to the merit of cutting the cables."
translations.idiomatic: At the victory feast next day Sun Quan toasted Dong Xi: "We owe this gathering to the man who cut those cables."

sentences.zh: 曹公出濡須，襲從權赴之，使襲督五樓船住濡須口。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao came out to Ruxu, Xi followed Quan to answer him; Quan ordered Xi to command five-deck ships stationed at the mouth of Ruxu.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao moved on Ruxu, Dong Xi followed Sun Quan and was told to hold five-deck ships at the estuary.

sentences.zh: 夜卒暴風，五樓船傾覆，左右散走舸，乞使襲出。

translations.literal: At night a sudden gale struck; the five-deck ships capsized; attendants scattered into small boats and begged that Xi be allowed out.
translations.idiomatic: A night squall capsized the tower ships; crewmen fled into skiffs and pleaded with Dong Xi to abandon ship.

sentences.zh: 襲怒曰：「受將軍任，在此備賊，何等委去也，敢復言此者斬！

translations.literal: Xi angrily said: "I received the general's charge to stand here against the enemy—what sort of thing is it to cast duty aside? Who speaks of leaving again will be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xi roared: "The general left me here to hold the line—what officer walks away? Mention retreat again and I kill you!"

sentences.zh: 」於是莫敢干。

translations.literal: Thereupon none dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared argue.

sentences.zh: 其夜船敗，襲死。

translations.literal: That night the ship was lost and Xi died.
translations.idiomatic: The hull broke apart that night and Dong Xi drowned.

sentences.zh: 權改服臨殯，供給甚厚。

translations.literal: Quan changed into mourning dress and attended the funeral rites; the provision was very generous.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wore mourning, attended the laying-out himself, and spared no expense.

sentences.zh: 甘寧字興霸，巴郡臨江人也。

translations.literal: Gan Ning, courtesy name Xingba, was a man of Linjiang in Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning, styled Xingba, came from Linjiang in Ba commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：寧本南陽人，其先客於巴郡。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: Ning was originally a man of Nanyang; his ancestors had sojourned in Ba commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu notes he was Nanyang-born but his family had long lived in Ba.

sentences.zh: 寧爲吏舉計掾，補蜀郡丞，頃之，棄官歸家。〉

translations.literal: He served as a clerk, was promoted accounting aide, and supplemented as assistant to the Shu commandery prefect; shortly thereafter he abandoned office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through clerk posts to aide in Shu commandery, then resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 少有氣力，好游俠，招合輕薄少年，爲之渠帥；

translations.literal: From youth he had strength and vigor; he loved knight-errantry, gathered reckless young men, and became their chieftain;
translations.idiomatic: Strong and adventurous from boyhood, he led a band of street youths as their chief;

sentences.zh: 羣聚相隨，挾持弓弩，負毦帶鈴，民聞鈴聲，即知是寧。

translations.literal: they banded together in groups, carried crossbows, wore yak tails and bells at the belt—when people heard the bells they knew it was Ning.
translations.idiomatic: they roamed with crossbows, bells, and yak-plume ornaments—at the jingle of bells everyone knew Gan Ning had come.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：寧輕俠殺人，藏舍亡命，聞於郡中。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: Ning in knight fashion killed men, harbored fugitives, and was notorious in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu adds that he killed in brawls, hid outlaws, and was infamous across the district.

sentences.zh: 其出入，步則陳車騎，水則連輕舟，侍從被文繡，所如光道路，住止常以繒錦維舟，去或割棄，以示奢也。〉

translations.literal: When he went abroad, on foot he arrayed chariots and riders; on water he linked light boats; attendants were clad in figured silk; wherever he passed he lit up the road; when he halted he always moored with silk brocade, and sometimes cut and cast it away on leaving to display extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: On land he paraded carriages and escorts; on water he ran a flotilla of light craft with attendants in brocade so bright it lit the shore—he even tied his boats with silk and cut it loose to flaunt his wealth.

sentences.zh: 人與相逢，及屬城長吏，接待隆厚者乃與交歡；

translations.literal: When people met him, and chief clerks of dependent cities—those who received him with generous courtesy he befriended;
translations.idiomatic: Travelers and county magistrates who welcomed him generously won his friendship;

sentences.zh: 不爾，即放所將奪其資貨，於長吏界中有所賊害，作其發負，至二十餘年。

translations.literal: otherwise he let loose his followers to seize their goods; within the chief clerks' jurisdictions he inflicted harm and left blame—this for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who did not felt his gang loot their goods; for twenty years he terrorized officials across several counties.

sentences.zh: 止不攻劫，頗讀諸子，乃往依劉表，因居南陽，不見進用，後轉託黃祖，祖又以凡人畜之。

translations.literal: He ceased raiding only after reading somewhat among the philosophers; then he went to rely on Liu Biao and dwelt at Nanyang, but was not promoted; later he attached himself to Huang Zu, who kept him like any ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: He finally quit brigandage after reading the masters, sought Liu Biao at Nanyang, found no office, then attached to Huang Zu, who treated him as a nobody.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：寧將僮客八百人就劉表。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: Ning led eight hundred retainers to Liu Biao.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu says he brought eight hundred clients to Liu Biao.

sentences.zh: 表儒人，不習軍事。

translations.literal: Biao was a scholar; he was not versed in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao was a bookish man with little grasp of war.

sentences.zh: 時諸英豪各各起兵，寧觀表事勢，終必無成，恐一朝土崩，并受其禍，欲東入吳。

translations.literal: At that time each hero raised troops in turn; Ning observed Biao's situation and concluded he would surely accomplish nothing; he feared that once it collapsed in a morning he would share in the disaster; he wished to go east into Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Watching heroes rise everywhere, Gan Ning decided Liu Biao would fail and that staying meant dying in the wreckage—he meant to cross east to Wu.

sentences.zh: 黃祖在夏口，軍不得過，乃留依祖，三年不禮之。

translations.literal: Huang Zu held Xiakou; the army could not pass; therefore he stayed relying on Zu, who for three years treated him without courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu blocked Xiakou, so Gan Ning had to stay under him and endure three years of cold neglect.

sentences.zh: 權討祖，祖軍敗奔走，追兵急，寧以善射，將兵在後，射殺校尉凌操。

translations.literal: When Quan campaigned against Zu, Zu's army was defeated and fled; pursuit was urgent; Ning, being skilled at shooting, led troops in the rear and shot dead Colonel Ling Cao.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan attacked, Huang Zu's line broke; Gan Ning rearguarded with the bow and killed Colonel Ling Cao.

sentences.zh: 祖旣得免，軍罷還營，待寧如初。

translations.literal: After Zu had escaped, the army ceased and returned to camp; he treated Ning as before.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huang Zu had escaped, he called off the pursuit and treated Gan Ning as he always had.

sentences.zh: 祖都督蘇飛數薦寧，祖不用，令人化誘其客，客稍亡。

translations.literal: Zu's area commander Su Fei repeatedly recommended Ning; Zu would not employ him and sent men to turn his followers by enticement; the followers gradually slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: Area commander Su Fei urged Huang Zu to use Gan Ning in vain; Huang Zu tried to poach his followers instead, and they drifted off.

sentences.zh: 寧欲去，恐不獲免，獨憂悶不知所出。

translations.literal: Ning wished to leave but feared he would not obtain safe departure; alone he was anxious and depressed and knew no way out.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning wanted to defect but feared capture; he brooded with no plan.

sentences.zh: 飛知其意，乃要寧，爲之置酒，謂曰：「吾薦子者數矣，主不能用。

translations.literal: Fei knew his intent; then he invited Ning, set out wine for him, and said: "I have recommended you repeatedly; the lord will not use you.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fei saw his mind, hosted him with wine, and said, "I have argued for you again and again; our lord will not listen.

sentences.zh: 日月逾邁，人生幾何，宜自遠圖，庶遇知己。

translations.literal: Sun and moon hurry on—human life is short—ought you not plan far ahead and perhaps meet a true patron?"
translations.idiomatic: The years race by—plan for yourself now so you may find a lord who values you."

sentences.zh: 」寧良乆乃曰：「雖有其志，未知所由。

translations.literal: Ning after a long while said: "Though I have that intent, I do not know the means."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning said after a pause, "I feel the same but see no path."

sentences.zh: 」飛曰：「吾欲白子爲邾長，於是去就，孰與臨阪轉丸乎？

translations.literal: Fei said: "I wish to report you as chief of Zhu—then staying or going, how does that compare to rolling a pellet on a slope?"
translations.idiomatic: Su Fei answered, "Let me get you made magistrate of Zhu—would that not beat drifting downhill like a stone?"

sentences.zh: 」寧曰：「幸甚。

translations.literal: Ning said: "Very fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: "Nothing could be better," said Gan Ning.

sentences.zh: 」飛白祖，聽寧之縣。

translations.literal: Fei reported to Zu; Zu permitted Ning to go to the county.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fei persuaded Huang Zu to send Gan Ning to that county.

sentences.zh: 招懷亡客并義從者，得數百人。〉

translations.literal: He summoned and soothed fugitive followers together with willing companions and obtained several hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: There Gan Ning rallied runaway clients and volunteers until he had several hundred fighters.

sentences.zh: 於是歸吳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Then he crossed to Wu.

sentences.zh: 周瑜、呂蒙皆共薦達，孫權加異，同於舊臣。

translations.literal: Zhou Yu and Lü Meng jointly recommended and advanced him; Sun Quan treated him with unusual favor, equal to old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yu and Lü Meng pressed his case, and Sun Quan honored him like a veteran councillor.

sentences.zh: 寧陳計曰：「今漢祚日微，曹操彌憍，終爲篡盜。

translations.literal: Ning presented a plan: "Now the Han mandate fades daily; Cao Cao grows ever more arrogant—in the end he will usurp and steal.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning advised: "The house of Han is failing and Cao Cao grows bold—he means to steal the throne.

sentences.zh: 南荊之地。

translations.literal: The southern Jingzhou lands.
translations.idiomatic: South Jingzhou

sentences.zh: 山陵形便，江川流通，誠是國之西勢也。

translations.literal: Mountain ridges offer favorable terrain and great rivers run through—truly the western strategic posture of the state.
translations.idiomatic: offer hills that shield and rivers that link—the western bastion of any southern realm.

sentences.zh: 寧已觀劉表，慮旣不遠，兒子又劣，非能承業傳基者也。

translations.literal: Ning has observed Liu Biao: his plans are not far-reaching, and his sons are moreover inferior—not men able to inherit and transmit the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao is shortsighted and his sons are worse—none can hold his legacy.

sentences.zh: 至尊當早規之，不可後操圖之。

translations.literal: You ought early to plan for this; you cannot wait until after Cao plans it.
translations.idiomatic: You must move before Cao Cao seizes the initiative."

sentences.zh: 圖之之計，宜先取黃祖。

translations.literal: The plan to take it ought to begin with Huang Zu.
translations.idiomatic: Begin with Huang Zu.

sentences.zh: 祖今年老，昏耄已甚，財穀並乏，左右欺弄，務於貨利，侵求吏士，吏士心怨，舟船戰具頓廢不脩，怠於耕農，軍無法伍。

translations.literal: Zu is now old, confused and senile in the extreme; wealth and grain are both exhausted; those around him deceive and manipulate; they pursue profit alone, encroach on officers and soldiers—the officers and soldiers resent them; boats and battle gear lie ruined and unrepaired; they are idle in farming and husbandry; the army lacks proper formations.
translations.idiomatic: He is ancient and muddled, short of money and grain; his staff cheats him, squeezes the troops for profit, and lets ships rot while soldiers starve—his host is demoralized and ill-drilled.

sentences.zh: 至尊今往，其破可必。

translations.literal: If you go now, his defeat can be certain.
translations.idiomatic: March now and you will crush him.

sentences.zh: 一破祖軍，鼓行而西，西據楚關，大勢彌廣，即可漸規巴蜀。

translations.literal: Once Zu's army is broken, march west with drums beating; seize the Chu Pass in the west—the great momentum grows broader—and then you may gradually plan Ba and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Break Huang Zu, wheel west, hold the Chu gates, and you open the road toward Ba and Shu."

sentences.zh: 」權深納之。

translations.literal: Quan deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan took the plan to heart.

sentences.zh: 張昭時在坐，難曰：「吳下業業，若軍果行，恐必致亂。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao was seated there and objected: "The lands of Wu are anxious and industrious; if the army indeed marches, I fear it will surely bring disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao objected: "Our people are already strained—a campaign could spark turmoil."

sentences.zh: 」寧謂昭曰：「國家以蕭何之任付君，君居守而憂亂，奚以希慕古人乎？

translations.literal: Ning said to Zhao: "The state entrusts you with the duty of Xiao He—yet you stay to guard and worry about disorder—with what then do you aspire to imitate the ancients?"
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning shot back: "The lord left you his rear area like Xiao He—if guarding home frightens you, how do you dare invoke the ancients?"

sentences.zh: 」權舉酒屬寧曰：「興霸，今年行討，如此酒矣，決以付卿。

translations.literal: Quan raised wine toward Ning and said: "Xingba, this year's campaign shall be like this wine—I resolve to entrust it to you.
