translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan raised his cup to Gan Ning: "Xingba, this year's war shall go down like this cup—I give it to you."

sentences.zh: 卿但當勉建方略，令必克祖，則卿之功，何嫌張長史之言乎。

translations.literal: You need only strive to devise strategy so that Zu is surely taken—then your merit—why resent Chief Clerk Zhang's words?"
translations.idiomatic: Plot until Huang Zu falls; once he does, Zhang Zhao's fears will mean nothing."

sentences.zh: 」權遂西，果禽祖，盡獲其士衆。

translations.literal: Quan then went west and indeed captured Zu, taking all his soldiers and masses.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan marched west, took Huang Zu, and absorbed his army.

sentences.zh: 遂授寧兵，屯當口

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted Ning troops and garrisoned Dangkou.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Gan Ning a command and posted him at Dangkou.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：初，權破祖，先作兩函，欲以盛祖及蘇飛首。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: At first, when Quan had broken Zu, he first made two chests, intending to hold Zu's and Su Fei's heads.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu says Sun Quan had two boxes ready for Huang Zu's head and Su Fei's.

sentences.zh: 飛令人告急於寧，寧曰：「飛若不言，吾豈忘之？

translations.literal: Fei ordered someone urgently report to Ning; Ning said: "If Fei had not spoken, could I have forgotten?"
translations.idiomatic: Su Fei begged Gan Ning for help; Gan Ning said, "Even without your plea I would not forget you."

sentences.zh: 」權爲諸將置酒，寧下席叩頭，血涕交流，爲權言：「飛疇昔舊恩，寧不值飛，固已損骸於溝壑，不得致命於麾下。

translations.literal: Quan set a feast for the generals; Ning left his mat, knocked his head until blood and tears mingled, and said to Quan: "Fei in former times showed me kindness; if Ning had not met Fei, my bones would already lie in gullies—I could not have devoted my life beneath your banner.
translations.idiomatic: At Sun Quan's banquet for the generals Gan Ning left his seat, bloodied his brow weeping, and said, "Su Fei raised me; without him I would rot in a ditch instead of serving you."

sentences.zh: 今飛罪當夷戮，特從將軍乞其首領。

translations.literal: Now Fei's crime deserves execution; I specially beg the general for his life."
translations.idiomatic: He deserves death by law, yet I beg you for his life."

sentences.zh: 」權感其言，謂曰：「今爲君致之，若走去何？

translations.literal: Quan was moved by his words and said to him: "Now I obtain him for you—if he flees, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan was moved and asked, "I spare him for you—but if he runs?"

sentences.zh: 」寧曰：「飛免分裂之禍，受更生之恩，逐之尚必不走，豈當圖亡哉！

translations.literal: Ning said: "If Fei is spared the disaster of being quartered and receives the kindness of renewed life, even if driven away he surely will not flee—how should he plot escape!
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning swore, "You spare him execution—he owes you rebirth. Drive him off and he still will not run—why would he flee?

sentences.zh: 若爾，寧頭當代入函。

translations.literal: If it be otherwise, let Ning's head take his place in the chest."
translations.idiomatic: If I am wrong, take my head instead."

sentences.zh: 」權乃赦之。〉

translations.literal: Quan thereupon pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan pardoned Su Fei.

sentences.zh: 後隨周瑜拒破曹公於烏林。

translations.literal: Later he followed Zhou Yu to resist and defeat Cao Cao at Wulin.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhou Yu to break Cao Cao at Wulin.

sentences.zh: 攻曹仁於南郡，未拔，寧建計先徑進取夷陵，往即得其城，因入守之。

translations.literal: He attacked Cao Ren in Nan commandery; it was not yet taken; Ning devised a plan first to advance directly and take Yiling—arriving he immediately obtained that city and thus entered and defended it.
translations.idiomatic: While Nan commandery still held out, Gan Ning rushed Yiling, seized it at once, and dug in.

sentences.zh: 時手下有數百兵，并所新得，僅滿千人。

translations.literal: At the time his subordinates numbered only several hundred troops, together with those newly obtained—barely a full thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He had only a few hundred men plus new recruits—scarcely a thousand all told.

sentences.zh: 曹仁乃令五六千人圍寧。

translations.literal: Cao Ren then ordered five or six thousand men to surround Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ren threw five or six thousand men around the town.

sentences.zh: 寧受攻累日，敵設高樓，雨射城中，士衆皆懼，惟寧談笑自若。

translations.literal: Ning endured attack many days; the enemy raised tall towers and rained shots into the city; officers and men were all afraid—only Ning talked and laughed at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The siege went on for days; Wei built towers and filled the walls with arrows—everyone trembled except Gan Ning, who joked through it.

sentences.zh: 遣使報瑜，瑜用呂蒙計，帥諸將解圍。

translations.literal: He sent a messenger to report to Yu; Yu employed Lü Meng's plan and led the generals to lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached Zhou Yu, who used Lü Meng's plan to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 後隨魯肅鎮益陽，拒關羽。

translations.literal: Later he followed Lu Su to garrison Yiyang and resist Guan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Lu Su at Yiyang against Guan Yu.

sentences.zh: 羽號有三萬人，自擇選銳士五千人，投縣上流十餘里淺瀨，云欲夜涉渡。

translations.literal: Yu claimed thirty thousand men; he personally selected five thousand crack troops and cast them upstream of the county more than ten li at a shallow ford, saying he wished to ford by night.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu claimed thirty thousand men and picked five thousand elites for a night ford above the county at a shoal.

sentences.zh: 肅與諸將議。

translations.literal: Su deliberated with the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su called a council.

sentences.zh: 寧時有三百兵，乃曰：「可復以五百人益吾，吾往對之，保羽聞吾欬唾，不敢涉水，涉水即是吾禽。

translations.literal: Ning at the time had three hundred troops; then he said: "Add five hundred more men for me and I will go oppose him—I guarantee that when Yu hears my cough and spit he will not dare cross the water—if he crosses the water he is my prisoner."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning had three hundred men and said, "Give me five hundred more and I will face him—Guan Yu will not dare wet his boots when he hears I am here."

sentences.zh: 」肅便選千兵益寧，寧乃夜往。

translations.literal: Su then selected a thousand troops to reinforce Ning; Ning then went by night.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Su gave him a thousand and Gan Ning moved by night.

sentences.zh: 羽聞之，住不渡，而結柴營，今遂名此處爲關羽瀨。

translations.literal: When Yu heard it, he halted and did not cross, but tied a brushwood camp; today this place is therefore named Guan Yu Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Yu stopped cold, threw up a brushwood camp, and the shoal is still called Guan Yu Ford.

sentences.zh: 權嘉寧功，拜西陵太守，領陽新、下雉兩縣。

translations.literal: Quan praised Ning's merit, appointed him Prefect of Xiling, and concurrently held Yangxin and Xiazhi counties.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan praised the deed, named him prefect of Xiling, and added Yangxin and Xiazhi.

sentences.zh: 後從攻皖，爲升城督。

translations.literal: Later he followed the attack on Wan and became commander of the assault on the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the assault on Wan as commander of the escalade.

sentences.zh: 寧手持練，身緣城，爲吏士先，卒破獲朱光。

translations.literal: Ning held a rope in hand, climbed the wall with his body, and led officers and soldiers; in the end they broke and captured Zhu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning scaled the wall on a rope ahead of his men and helped seize Zhu Guang.

sentences.zh: 計功，呂蒙爲最。

translations.literal: When merit was reckoned, Lü Meng was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng took first credit for the storm.

sentences.zh: 寧次之，拜折衝將軍。

translations.literal: Ning was next; he was appointed General Who Smashes the Enemy's Battle Line.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning ranked second and became general who smashes the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 後曹公出濡須，寧爲前部督，受勑出斫敵前營。

translations.literal: Later when Cao Cao came out to Ruxu, Ning was vanguard commander and received orders to go strike the enemy's forward camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao returned to Ruxu, Gan Ning led the van under orders to raid the forward camp.

sentences.zh: 權特賜米酒衆殽，寧乃料賜手下百餘人食。

translations.literal: Quan specially granted rice wine and many dishes; Ning then portioned it out to grant food to more than a hundred subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent rice wine and viands; Gan Ning shared them with more than a hundred picked men.

sentences.zh: 食畢，寧先以銀盌酌酒，自飲兩盌，乃酌與其都督。

translations.literal: When they had finished eating, Ning first poured wine in a silver bowl, drank two bowls himself, then poured for his area commander.
translations.idiomatic: When they had eaten, he poured two bowls of wine from a silver cup for himself, then offered one to his deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 都督伏，不肯時持。

translations.literal: The area commander prostrated himself and would not take it in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: The man knelt and refused the cup.

sentences.zh: 寧引白削置膝上，呵謂之曰：「卿見知於至尊，孰與甘寧？

translations.literal: Ning drew a white blade and placed it on his knee, shouted and said to him: "You are seen and favored by the Supreme—how does that compare to Gan Ning?
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning laid a bare blade on his knee and barked, "The sovereign favors you—does that outrank me?

sentences.zh: 甘寧尚不惜死，卿何以獨惜死乎？

translations.literal: Gan Ning still does not spare death—why do you alone spare death?"
translations.idiomatic: I do not fear death—why do you cling to yours?"

sentences.zh: 」都督見寧色厲，即起拜待酒次，通酌兵各一銀盌。

translations.literal: When the area commander saw Ning's expression fierce, he immediately rose, bowed, awaited his turn with the wine, and passed to pour for each soldier one silver bowl.
translations.idiomatic: The officer sprang up, drained his cup, and passed silver bowls down the ranks.

sentences.zh: 至二更時，銜枚出斫敵。

translations.literal: At the second watch they went out with mouth-plugs and struck the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At second watch they muffled their mouths and hit the camp.

sentences.zh: 敵驚動，遂退。

translations.literal: The enemy was alarmed and stirred; then they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wei panicked and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 寧益貴重，增兵二千人。

translations.literal: Ning became increasingly honored and weighty; his troops were increased by two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan prized Gan Ning still more and added two thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 〈《江表傳》曰：「曹公出濡須，號步騎四十萬，臨江飲馬。

translations.literal: 《Accounts from Beyond the Yangzi》 says: "When Cao Cao came out to Ruxu, he claimed four hundred thousand infantry and cavalry and watered his horses along the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan says Cao Cao brought four hundred thousand foot and horse to Ruxu and watered them along the Yangzi."

sentences.zh: 權率衆七萬應之，使寧領三千人爲前部督。

translations.literal: Quan led seventy thousand men to answer him and ordered Ning to lead three thousand men as vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan met him with seventy thousand men and made Gan Ning vanguard with three thousand.

sentences.zh: 權密勑寧，使夜入魏軍。

translations.literal: Quan secretly ordered Ning to enter the Wei army by night.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly told Gan Ning to infiltrate Wei by night.

sentences.zh: 寧乃選手下健兒百餘人，徑詣曹公營下，使拔鹿角，踰壘入營，斬得數十級。

translations.literal: Ning then selected more than a hundred stalwart followers among his subordinates, went straight to below Cao Cao's camp, ordered the deer-horn stakes pulled up, scaled the ramparts and entered the camp, and beheaded several tens of heads.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning took a hundred shock troops to Cao Cao's lines, tore down the palisade stakes, vaulted the wall, and came back with dozens of heads.

sentences.zh: 北軍驚駭鼓譟，舉火如星，寧已還入營，作鼓吹，稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The northern army panicked and clamored; fires sprang up like stars; Ning had already returned to camp, sounded drums and pipes, and shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei troops erupted in panic—watchfires flared like stars—but Gan Ning was already back in Wu lines sounding victory drums.

sentences.zh: 因夜見權，權喜曰：「足以驚駭老子否？

translations.literal: Then by night he saw Quan; Quan happily said: "Enough to startle the old man?"
translations.idiomatic: He reported that night; Sun Quan grinned, "Did that give Old Cao a jolt?"

sentences.zh: 聊以觀卿膽耳。

translations.literal: I merely wished to take a look at your gall."
translations.idiomatic: I only wanted to see your nerve."

sentences.zh: 」即賜絹千匹，刀百口。

translations.literal: He immediately granted a thousand bolts of silk and a hundred knives.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan gave him a thousand bolts of silk and a hundred blades.

sentences.zh: 權曰：「孟德有張遼，孤有興霸，足相敵也。

translations.literal: Quan said: "Mengde has Zhang Liao; I have Xingba—enough to match him."
translations.idiomatic: "Cao Cao keeps Zhang Liao; I keep you, Xingba—that evens the scales."

sentences.zh: 」停住月餘，北軍便退。〉

translations.literal: They halted for just over a month; then the northern army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After a month-long standoff the northern army lifted camp and left.

sentences.zh: 寧雖麤猛好殺，然開爽有計略，輕財敬士，能厚養健兒，健兒亦樂爲用命。

translations.literal: Though Ning was crude, fierce, and fond of killing, he was open and frank, possessed stratagem, slighted wealth and respected gentlemen, could richly nurture stalwart fighters, and the stalwart fighters too gladly obeyed unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Violent and eager to kill, Gan Ning was also shrewd and generous to scholars; his picked warriors served him to the death.

sentences.zh: 建安二十年，從攻合肥，會疫疾，軍旅皆已引出，唯車下虎士千餘人，并呂蒙、蔣欽、凌統及寧，從權逍遙津北。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Jian'an he followed the attack on Hefei; there was an epidemic and the army columns had all been led out; only more than a thousand tiger guards under the chariot, together with Lü Meng, Jiang Qin, Ling Tong, and Ning, accompanied Quan north of Xiaoyao Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 20, sickness had pulled most men from Hefei; only a thousand household guards with Lü Meng, Jiang Qin, Ling Tong, and Gan Ning escorted Sun Quan north of Xiaoyao Ford.

sentences.zh: 張遼覘望知之，即將步騎奄至。

translations.literal: Zhang Liao observed and realized it; then led infantry and cavalry to arrive suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Liao spotted the isolated party and swept down with horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 寧引弓射敵，與統等死戰。

translations.literal: Ning drew his bow and shot at the enemy; together with Tong and others he fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning shot back while he and Ling Tong fought for their lives.

sentences.zh: 寧厲聲問鼓吹何以不作，壯氣毅然，權尤嘉之。

translations.literal: Ning asked in a stern voice why the drum and wind music was not played; his bold spirit was firm and resolute; Quan especially praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning roared for the band to strike up—his defiance thrilled the line—and Sun Quan admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：凌統怨寧殺其父操，寧常備統，不與相見。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: Ling Tong resented Ning for killing his father Cao; Ning constantly guarded against Tong and did not meet him.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu says Ling Tong blamed Gan Ning for killing Ling Cao; Gan Ning kept clear of him.

sentences.zh: 權亦命統不得讎之。

translations.literal: Quan also ordered Tong not to take revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan forbade a blood feud.

sentences.zh: 甞於呂蒙舍會，酒酣，統乃以刀舞。

translations.literal: Once they met at Lü Meng's house; when the wine ran deep, Tong then danced with a knife.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in Lü Meng's house, with cups heavy, Ling Tong began a knife dance.

sentences.zh: 寧起曰：「寧能雙戟舞。

translations.literal: Ning rose and said: "Ning can dance twin halberds."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning stood and offered a paired-halberd dance.

sentences.zh: 」蒙曰：「寧雖能，未若蒙之巧也。

translations.literal: Meng said: "Though Ning can, it is not as skillful as Meng."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng said Gan Ning could perform but not as deftly as he.

sentences.zh: 」因操刀持楯，以身分之。

translations.literal: Therefore he took knife and shield and with his body separated them.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped between them with blade and shield.

sentences.zh: 後權知統意，因令寧將兵，遂徙屯於半州。〉

translations.literal: Later Quan understood Tong's intent; therefore he ordered Ning to command troops and transferred the garrison to Banzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Ling Tong's hatred, Sun Quan split the commands and moved Gan Ning to camp at Banzhou.

sentences.zh: 寧厨下兒曾有過，走投呂蒙。

translations.literal: A kitchen servant of Ning's once faulted and fled to seek Lü Meng.
translations.idiomatic: One of Gan Ning's kitchen boys offended him and fled to Lü Meng.

sentences.zh: 蒙恐寧殺之，故不即還。

translations.literal: Meng feared Ning would kill him; therefore he did not return him immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng hid the boy, fearing Gan Ning would kill him.

sentences.zh: 後寧齎禮禮蒙母，臨當與升堂，乃出厨下兒還寧。

translations.literal: Later Ning presented gifts honoring Meng's mother; when they were about to ascend the hall together, he then produced the kitchen boy and returned him to Ning.
translations.idiomatic: When Gan Ning came with gifts for Lü Meng's mother, Lü Meng handed back the servant only as they were about to enter the hall.

sentences.zh: 寧許蒙不殺。

translations.literal: Ning promised Meng he would not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning swore to Lü Meng he would spare the boy.

sentences.zh: 斯須還船，縛置桑樹，自挽弓射殺之。

translations.literal: A moment later, back on his boat, he tied him to a mulberry tree, drew his bow himself, and shot him dead.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later aboard his boat he lashed the servant to a mulberry and shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 畢，勑船人更增舸纜，解衣卧船中。

translations.literal: When finished, he ordered the boatmen to add more hawser to the skiffs, removed his clothes, and lay in the middle of the boat.
translations.idiomatic: Then he ordered extra mooring lines, stripped, and stretched out in the hold.

sentences.zh: 蒙大怒，擊鼓會兵，欲就船攻寧。

translations.literal: Meng was greatly angry, beat the drums and assembled troops, and wished to go to the boat and attack Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng beat assembly drums and meant to storm Gan Ning's boat.

sentences.zh: 寧聞之，故卧不起。

translations.literal: When Ning heard it, he purposely lay down and did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning heard but stayed prone and refused to rise.

sentences.zh: 蒙母徒跣出諫蒙曰：「至尊待汝如骨肉，屬汝以大事，何有以私怒而欲攻殺甘寧？

translations.literal: Meng's mother went barefoot out to remonstrate with Meng, saying: "The Supreme treats you like flesh and bone and entrusts you with great affairs—how can you from private anger wish to attack and kill Gan Ning?"
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng's mother ran out barefoot: "The sovereign trusts you as kin and charges you with weighty duty—would you murder Gan Ning from spite?"

sentences.zh: 寧死之日，縱至尊不問，汝是爲臣下非法。

translations.literal: On the day Ning dies, even if the Supreme does not investigate, you as a minister below act unlawfully."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the court forgave you, a subject may not settle private scores."

sentences.zh: 」蒙素至孝，聞母言，即豁然意釋，自至寧舩，笑呼之曰：「興霸，老母待卿食，急上！

translations.literal: Meng was always extremely filial; hearing his mother's words, his meaning opened and he released his anger; he himself went to Ning's boat, laughed and called to him: "Xingba—the old mother waits for you to eat; hurry up!"
translations.idiomatic: The dutiful Lü Meng yielded; he boarded Gan Ning's craft laughing, "Xingba—Mother has supper waiting—come now!"

sentences.zh: 」寧涕泣歔欷曰：「負卿。

translations.literal: Ning wept and sobbed and said: "I have wronged you."
translations.idiomatic: Gan Ning wept, "I failed you."

sentences.zh: 」與蒙俱還見母，歡宴竟日。

translations.literal: Together with Meng he returned to see the mother, and they feasted happily all day.
translations.idiomatic: They returned with Lü Meng and feasted with her all day.

sentences.zh: 寧卒，權痛惜之。

translations.literal: When Ning died, Quan deeply mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gan Ning died, Sun Quan grieved deeply.

sentences.zh: 子瓌，以罪徙會稽，無幾死。

translations.literal: His son Gui, because of a crime, was banished to Kuaiji; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gui was banished to Kuaiji for crime and died soon after.

sentences.zh: 凌統字公績，吳郡餘杭人也。

translations.literal: Ling Tong, courtesy name Gongji, was a man of Yuhang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tong, styled Gongji, came from Yuhang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 父操，輕俠有膽氣，孫策初興，每從征伐，常冠軍履鋒。

translations.literal: His father Cao was a knight-errant with courage; when Sun Ce first rose, he always followed on campaigns, constantly leading the van and treading the blades.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ling Cao was a fearless rover who spearheaded Sun Ce's campaigns.

sentences.zh: 守永平長，平治山越，姦猾斂手，遷破賊校尉。

translations.literal: He guarded as chief of Yongping, pacified and governed the Shanyue; the crafty folded their hands; he was promoted Colonel Who Breaks the Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: As chief of Yongping he subdued the Shanyue and rose to colonel who breaks bandits.

sentences.zh: 及權統軍，從討江夏。

translations.literal: When Quan commanded the army, he followed the campaign against Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Sun Quan's Jiangxia expedition.

sentences.zh: 入夏口，先登，破其前鋒，輕舟獨進，中流矢死。

translations.literal: They entered Xiakou; he was first to climb; he broke their vanguard; in a light boat he advanced alone and died to an arrow midstream.
translations.idiomatic: He was first into Xiakou, shattered the vanguard in a light boat, and fell to an arrow midstream.

sentences.zh: 統年十五，左右多稱述者，權亦以操死國事，拜統別部司馬，行破賊都尉，使攝父兵。

translations.literal: Tong was fifteen sui; those around him often praised and described him; Quan also because Cao had died for state affairs appointed Tong Major of a Separate Division, acting Commandant Who Breaks the Bandits, and ordered him to hold his father's troops for the nonce.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Ling Tong was praised on every side; because Ling Cao had died for the state, Sun Quan made him major of a separate division and acting commandant who breaks bandits to lead his father's troops.

sentences.zh: 後從擊山賊，權破保屯先還，餘麻屯萬人，統與督張異等留攻圍之，克日當攻。

translations.literal: Later he followed the strike on mountain bandits; Quan broke the fortified camp and returned first; the remainder at Ma stockade were ten thousand men; Tong together with commander Zhang Yi and others stayed to attack and besiege them; a day was set for the assault.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan stormed a hill fort and withdrew, ten thousand bandits held Ma village; Ling Tong and commander Zhang Yi stayed to besiege them with a fixed assault date.

sentences.zh: 先期，統與督陳勤會飲酒，勤剛勇任氣，因督祭酒，陵轢一坐，舉罰不以其道。

translations.literal: Before the date, Tong together with commander Chen Qin met to drink wine; Qin was fierce and brave and indulged his temper; as supervisor of the sacrificial wine he rode roughshod over the whole seat and imposed penalties not according to fair usage.
translations.idiomatic: Before the attack Ling Tong drank with Chen Qin, who as toast-master bullied the table and imposed unfair drinking fines.

sentences.zh: 統疾其侮慢，靣折不爲用。

translations.literal: Tong hated his insult and arrogance and openly refused to obey.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tong called out his arrogance and refused his orders.

sentences.zh: 勤怒詈統，及其父操，統流涕不荅，衆因罷出。

translations.literal: Qin angrily cursed Tong and his father Cao; Tong wept and did not answer; the crowd therefore broke up and left.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qin reviled Ling Tong and his father; Ling Tong wept in silence and the party dispersed.

sentences.zh: 勤乘酒凶悖，又於道路辱統。

translations.literal: Qin, riding on wine, was fierce and contrary, and on the road again insulted Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, Chen Qin stopped Ling Tong on the road to humiliate him.

sentences.zh: 統不忍，引刀斫勤，數日乃死。

translations.literal: Tong could not bear it; he drew a knife and hacked Qin; after several days Qin died.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tong cut him down; Chen Qin lingered for days and died.

sentences.zh: 及當攻屯，統曰：「非死無以謝罪。

translations.literal: When the time came to attack the stockade, Tong said: "Unless I die I have no means to apologize for my guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Before the assault Ling Tong said only death could atone for killing Chen Qin.

sentences.zh: 」乃率厲士卒，身當矢石，所次一靣，應時披壞，諸將乘勝，遂大破之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he encouraged the soldiers, himself faced arrows and stones; the sector he attacked gave way at once; the generals rode the victory and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself at the wall under missile fire, breached a sector, and the army poured through for a rout.

sentences.zh: 還，自拘於軍正。

translations.literal: On return he bound himself to the army judge.
translations.idiomatic: He surrendered himself to military justice.

sentences.zh: 權壯其果毅，使得以功贖罪。

translations.literal: Quan praised his resolution and allowed him to redeem guilt with merit.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan admired his courage and let merit erase the crime.

sentences.zh: 後權復征江夏，統爲前鋒，與所厚健兒數十人共乘一船，常去大兵數十里。

translations.literal: Later Quan again campaigned against Jiangxia; Tong was vanguard; together with several tens of intimate stalwart fighters he rode one boat, often several tens of li separated from the main army.
translations.idiomatic: On the next Jiangxia campaign Ling Tong led the van in one boat with dozens of picked men, miles ahead of the main host.

sentences.zh: 行入右江，斬黃祖將張碩，盡獲船人。

translations.literal: Advancing into the right branch of the river, he beheaded Huang Zu's general Zhang Shuo and captured all the boat crews.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the right fork he slew Huang Zu's officer Zhang Shuo and seized his boat crews.

sentences.zh: 還以白權，引軍兼道，水陸並集。

translations.literal: He returned and reported to Quan; Quan led the army by forced marches; water and land forces gathered together.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to Sun Quan, who drove night marches by land and water.

sentences.zh: 時呂蒙敗其水軍，而統先搏其城，於是大獲。

translations.literal: At the time Lü Meng had defeated their water army, but Tong first grappled with its walls; therefore there was a great capture.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Meng smashed the fleet while Ling Tong stormed the walls; together they won decisively.

sentences.zh: 權以統爲承烈都尉，與周瑜等拒破曹公於烏林，遂攻曹仁，遷爲校尉。

translations.literal: Quan appointed Tong Commandant Who Bears the Flame; together with Zhou Yu and others he resisted and defeated Cao Cao at Wulin; then he attacked Cao Ren and was promoted colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named Ling Tong bearer-of-flame commandant; he helped Zhou Yu at Wulin, pressed Cao Ren, and rose to colonel.

sentences.zh: 雖在軍旅，親賢接士，輕財重義，有國士之風。

translations.literal: Though in military service, he drew near the worthy and received scholars; he slighted wealth and prized righteousness; he had the bearing of a knight of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the field he honored worthy men and prized honor over gold—a temper worthy of a champion.

sentences.zh: 又從破皖，拜盪寇中郎將，領沛相。

translations.literal: Again he followed the capture of Wan; he was appointed General of the Household Who Sweeps the Bandits (middle rank) and concurrently Administrator of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Wan, became middle general who sweeps bandits, and acting administrator of Pei commandery.

sentences.zh: 與呂蒙等西取三郡，反自益陽，從往合肥，爲右部督。

translations.literal: Together with Lü Meng and others he took three commanderies in the west; returning from Yiyang he followed toward Hefei and was commander of the right wing.
translations.idiomatic: With Lü Meng he seized three western commanderies, returned through Yiyang, then marched on Hefei as right-wing commander.

sentences.zh: 時權徹軍，前部已發，魏將張遼等奄至津北。

translations.literal: At the time Quan was withdrawing the army; the van had already departed; Wei general Zhang Liao and others suddenly arrived north of the ford.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's rear was pulling out when Zhang Liao slammed the north bank.

sentences.zh: 權使追還前兵，兵去已遠，勢不相及，統率親近三百人陷圍，扶扞權出。

translations.literal: Quan ordered the pursuit to recall the van; the van had already gone far and the situation could not reach; Tong led three hundred intimate guards into the siege, shielding and defending Quan out.
translations.idiomatic: Recall orders never caught the van; Ling Tong drove three hundred household guards through the ring to shield Sun Quan out.

sentences.zh: 敵已毀橋，橋之屬者兩版，權策馬驅馳，統復還戰，左右盡死，身亦被創，所殺數十人，度權已免，乃還。

translations.literal: The enemy had already destroyed the bridge; of the bridge's covering only two planks remained; Quan whipped his horse in gallop; Tong again returned to fight; those to his left and right all died; his body also suffered wounds; he killed several tens of men; estimating that Quan had already escaped, he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had smashed the bridge leaving two planks; Sun Quan spurred across while Ling Tong fought until every companion fell—he killed dozens, bleeding, and fell back once Sun Quan was safe.

sentences.zh: 橋敗路絕，統被甲潛行。

translations.literal: The bridge was ruined and the road cut off; Tong wore armor and slipped away on foot.
translations.idiomatic: With the bridge gone he crept through in armor.

sentences.zh: 權旣御船，見之驚喜。

translations.literal: Quan had already boarded the ship; when he saw him he was surprised and joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's boat had sailed when Ling Tong appeared—Sun Quan rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 統痛親近無反者，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: Tong grieved that none of his intimates had returned; sorrow overcame him.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tong wept that none of his men came back.

sentences.zh: 權引袂拭之，謂曰：「公績，亡者已矣，苟使卿在，何患無人？」

translations.literal: Quan pulled his sleeve and wiped him, saying to him: "Gongji, the dead are already gone; as long as you remain, why worry there are no men?"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wiped his tears: "Gongji, the fallen are gone; while you live I still have officers."

sentences.zh: 〈《吳書》曰：統創甚，權遂留統於舟，盡易其衣服。

translations.literal: 《Book of Wu》 says: Tong's wounds were very severe; Quan therefore kept Tong on the boat and completely changed his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wu says Ling Tong's wounds were grave; Sun Quan kept him aboard and gave him fresh clothes.

sentences.zh: 其創賴得卓氏良藥，故得不死。〉

translations.literal: His wounds owed their healing to the Zhuo family's fine medicine; therefore he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's patent medicine saved his life.

sentences.zh: 拜偏將軍，倍給本兵。

translations.literal: He was appointed Lieutenant General and given double his original troops.
translations.idiomatic: He became lieutenant general with twice his former command.

sentences.zh: 時有薦同郡盛暹於權者，以爲梗槩大節有過於統，權曰：「且令如統足矣。

translations.literal: At the time someone had recommended Sheng Xian of the same commandery to Quan, thinking his backbone and great integrity surpassed Tong's; Quan said: "For now, having him like Tong is enough."
translations.idiomatic: When a man praised Sheng Xian of his county as greater than Ling Tong, Sun Quan replied, "Another man like Ling Tong would already suffice."

sentences.zh: 」後召暹夜至，時統已卧，聞之，攝衣出門，執其手以入。

translations.literal: Later he summoned Xian to come by night; at the time Tong was already lying down; hearing it, he seized his clothes, went out the door, grasped his hand, and led him in.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned by night, Ling Tong rose from bed, pulled Sheng Xian inside hand in hand.

sentences.zh: 其愛善不害如此。

translations.literal: His love of the good and unwillingness to harm were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his zeal for worthy peers.

sentences.zh: 統以山中人尚多壯悍，可以威恩誘也，權令東占且討之，命勑屬城，凡統所求，皆先給後聞。

translations.literal: Tong because the mountain people were still many and stalwart and fierce, thought they could be enticed with awe and kindness; Quan ordered him east to occupy and campaign against them; he ordered dependent cities: whatever Tong requested, all were supplied first and reported afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing fierce hillfolk who might yield to kindness and fear, Sun Quan sent Ling Tong east with blank authority—every county supplied him before memorializing.

sentences.zh: 統素愛士，士亦慕焉。

translations.literal: Tong always loved soldiers; the soldiers also admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Tong loved his soldiers and they loved him.

sentences.zh: 得精兵萬餘人，過本縣，步入寺門，見長吏懷三版，恭敬盡禮，親舊故人，恩意益隆。

translations.literal: He obtained more than ten thousand crack troops; passing his native county, he walked in through the temple gate, saw the chief clerk embracing three tablets, was respectful in completing ritual; to kinsmen, old friends, and former acquaintances his kindness grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Leading ten thousand veterans he walked through his home canton to the clerk's office with tablets in hand, bowing with extra courtesy to kin and old friends.

sentences.zh: 事畢當出，會病卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: When affairs were finished he ought to have departed; he met death by illness; he was then forty-nine sui.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to leave office he died of illness at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 權聞之，拊牀起坐，哀不能自止，數日減膳，言及流涕，使張承爲作銘誄。

translations.literal: When Quan heard it, he slapped the couch and rose; grief could not stop itself; for several days he reduced meals; speaking of it brought flowing tears; he ordered Zhang Cheng to compose his inscription and dirge.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan smote his couch, fasted for days, wept whenever Ling Tong was named, and had Zhang Cheng write his elegy.

sentences.zh: 二子烈、封，年各數歲，權內養於宮，愛待與諸子同，賔客進見，呼示之曰：「此吾虎子也。

translations.literal: His two sons Lie and Feng were each several sui old; Quan raised them inside the palace; his love and treatment were the same as for his various sons; when guests came to audience he called and showed them, saying: "These are my tiger cubs."
translations.idiomatic: His young sons Lie and Feng Sun Quan raised in the palace like princes and showed to guests as his "tiger cubs."

sentences.zh: 」及八九歲，令葛光教之讀書，十日一令乘馬，追錄統功，封烈亭侯，還其故兵。

translations.literal: When they reached eight or nine sui, he ordered Ge Guang to teach them to read; once every ten days he ordered them to ride horses; he traced Ling Tong's merit, enfeoffed Lie as village marquis, and returned his original troops.
translations.idiomatic: At eight or nine Ge Guang taught them letters; every ten days they rode horses; Sun Quan recorded Ling Tong's merit, made Lie a village marquis, and restored his father's troops.

sentences.zh: 後烈有罪免，封復襲爵領兵。

translations.literal: Later Lie committed a crime and was stripped of rank; Feng again inherited the noble rank and commanded troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Lie lost his title for crime, Feng took the fief and command.

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：觀孫權之養士也，傾心竭思，以求其死力，泣周泰之夷，殉陳武之妾，請呂蒙之命，育凌統之孤，卑曲苦志，如此之勤也。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng said: "Observe how Sun Quan nurtured men of purpose—he poured out heart and thought to win their willingness to die; he wept over Zhou Tai's wounds, buried a concubine with Chen Wu, pleaded for Lü Meng's life, and raised Ling Tong's orphans—humble, earnest diligence like this."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng reflects that Sun Quan exhausted himself winning devotion—weeping for Zhou Tai, accompanying Chen Wu's concubine to the grave, begging Lü Meng's physician, raising Ling Tong's sons.

sentences.zh: 是故雖令德無聞，仁澤內著，而能屈彊荊吳，僭擬年歲者，抑有由也。

translations.literal: Therefore though his manifest virtue was not widely heard and humane grace showed chiefly within, he could yet bend strong foes in Jing and Wu and maintain a borrowed throne for years—there was a reason."
translations.idiomatic: Though Sun Quan lacked fame for virtue, his officers gave everything; that is how he held Wu for so long against great rivals.

sentences.zh: 然霸王之道，期於大者遠者，是以先王建德義之基，恢信順之宇，制經略之綱，明貴賤之叙，易簡而其親可乆，體全而其功可大，豈踒璅近務，邀利於當年哉？

translations.literal: Yet the way of a hegemon king aims at what is great and far; therefore the former kings established foundations of virtue and duty, expanded the realm of trust and obedience, set in place the net of strategy, clarified the order of noble and base—plain and whole so that kinship endures and merit can grow great. How could petty favors for the moment suffice?
translations.idiomatic: True kingship thinks generations ahead—foundations of trust and order—not favors traded for the hour.

sentences.zh: 語曰「雖小道，必有可觀者焉，致遠恐泥」，其是之謂乎！〉

translations.literal: The saying runs, "Even in small arts there is something worth seeing; applied to far ends it may bog down"—does it not speak to this?
translations.idiomatic: The Analects warn that petty skills muddy grand ventures—and Sun Quan proves the point.

sentences.zh: 徐盛字文嚮，琅邪莒人也。

translations.literal: Xu Sheng, courtesy name Wenxiang, was a man of Ju in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sheng, styled Wenxiang, came from Ju in Langya commandery.

sentences.zh: 遭亂，客居吳，以勇氣聞。

translations.literal: He encountered turmoil and dwelt as a guest in Wu; he became known for courage.
translations.idiomatic: Strife drove him to Wu, where his valor became known.

sentences.zh: 孫權統事，以爲別部司馬，授兵五百人，守柴桑長，拒黃祖。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan took charge of affairs, he appointed him Major of a Separate Division, gave five hundred troops, had him guard as chief of Chaisang, and resist Huang Zu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan made him major of a separate division with five hundred men as Chaisang chief against Huang Zu.

sentences.zh: 祖子射，甞率數千人下攻盛。

translations.literal: Zu's son She once led several thousand men downstream to attack Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu's son She once struck downward with thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 盛時吏士不滿二百，與相拒擊，傷射吏士千餘人。

translations.literal: At the time Sheng's officers and soldiers numbered fewer than two hundred; they resisted one another in combat and wounded more than a thousand of She's officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Sheng had fewer than two hundred men yet bloodied She for more than a thousand casualties.

sentences.zh: 已乃開門出戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Afterward he opened the gate and went out to battle and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Then he sallied and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 射遂絕迹不復爲寇。

translations.literal: She then vanished without trace and never again raided.
translations.idiomatic: She never raided again.

sentences.zh: 權以爲校尉、蕪湖令。

translations.literal: Quan appointed him colonel and magistrate of Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him colonel and magistrate of Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 復討臨城南阿山賊有功，徙中郎將，督校兵。

translations.literal: Again he campaigned against the mountain bandits south of Lincheng with merit; he was transferred to middle general and supervised training troops.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared bandits south of Lincheng, became middle general, and inspected training troops.

sentences.zh: 曹公出濡須，從權禦之。

translations.literal: When Cao Cao came out to Ruxu, he followed Quan to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Sun Quan against Cao Cao at Ruxu.

sentences.zh: 魏甞大出橫江，盛與諸將俱赴討。

translations.literal: Wei once sent a great force to Hengjiang; Sheng together with the various generals all went to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei massed at Hengjiang, Xu Sheng rode with the host.

sentences.zh: 時乘蒙衝，遇迅風，船落敵岸下，諸將恐懼，未有出者，盛獨將兵，上突斫敵，敵披退走，有所傷殺，風止便還，權大壯之。

translations.literal: At the time they rode covered swoopers; they met a sudden wind; the boat was driven onto the enemy shore below; the various generals feared and none went out; Sheng alone led troops, ascended, burst in, and chopped the enemy; the enemy broke and retreated; there were wounded and killed; when the wind stopped he returned; Quan greatly honored him.
translations.idiomatic: A gale drove Xu Sheng's tower ship onto Wei-held shore; others froze while he fought ashore, inflicted casualties, and withdrew when the wind dropped—Sun Quan acclaimed him.

sentences.zh: 及權爲魏稱藩，魏使邢貞拜權爲吳王。

translations.literal: When Quan declared himself a vassal to Wei, Wei's envoy Xing Zhen invested Quan as king of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan submitted to Wei as vassal, Wei sent Xing Zhen to invest him as king of Wu.

sentences.zh: 權出都亭候貞，貞有驕色，張昭旣怒，而盛忿憤，顧謂同列曰：「盛等不能奮身出命，爲國家并許洛，吞巴蜀，而令吾君與貞盟，不亦辱乎！

translations.literal: Quan went out to the Ducheng pavilion to await Zhen; Zhen had a proud expression; Zhang Zhao was already angry, while Sheng was indignant; he turned and said to those of his row: "We have been unable to stake our lives to swallow Xu and Luoyang and Ba and Shu for the state, yet we make our lord covenant with Zhen—is it not shameful!"
translations.idiomatic: At Ducheng pavilion Xing Zhen looked down on them; Zhang Zhao raged and Xu Sheng cried to his peers, "We have not conquered the north for our lord—yet we bind him to Xing Zhen—what shame!"

sentences.zh: 」因涕泣橫流。

translations.literal: Thereupon tears streamed across his face.
translations.idiomatic: Tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 貞聞之，謂其旅曰：「江東將相如此，非乆下人者也。」

translations.literal: When Zhen heard it, he said to his suite: "The generals and ministers of Jiangdong are thus—not long will they remain men below others."
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zhen told his escort, "Such spirit among Wu's ministers—they will not stay vassals forever."

sentences.zh: 後遷建武將軍，封都亭侯，領廬江太守，賜臨城縣爲奉邑。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted General Who Establishes Martial Might, enfeoffed village marquis of Ducheng, concurrently Prefect of Lujiang, and Lincheng county was granted as benefice revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general who establishes martial might, village marquis at Ducheng, Lujiang prefect, with Lincheng as benefice.

sentences.zh: 劉備次西陵，盛攻取諸屯，所向有功。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei encamped at Xiling, Sheng attacked and took the various garrisons; wherever he turned he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei camped at Xiling, Xu Sheng seized his outposts in succession.

sentences.zh: 曹休出洞口，盛與呂範、全琮渡江拒守。

translations.literal: When Cao Xiu came out at Dongkou, Sheng together with Lü Fan and Quan Zong crossed the river to resist and guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Xiu advanced at Dongkou, Xu Sheng crossed with Lü Fan and Quan Zong to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 遭大風，船人多喪，盛收餘兵，與休夾江。

translations.literal: They met a great wind; many men on the boats were lost; Sheng gathered the remnant troops and faced Xiu across the river.
translations.idiomatic: A gale sank crews; Xu Sheng rallied survivors and faced Cao Xiu across the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 休使兵將就船攻盛，盛以少禦多，敵不能克，各引軍退。

translations.literal: Xiu ordered troops to board ships and attack Sheng; Sheng with few opposed many; the enemy could not overcome him; each side led troops away.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiu tried shipborne assaults; Xu Sheng held outnumbered until Wei withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷安東將軍，封蕪湖侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Pacifies the East and enfeoffed marquis of Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: He became pacifying-east general and marquis of Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 後魏文帝大出，有渡江之志，盛建計從建業築圍，作薄落，圍上設假樓，江中浮船。

translations.literal: Later Wei Wendi mounted a great expedition with intent to cross the river; Sheng devised a plan to build an enclosure from Jianye, make thin palisades, set dummy towers atop the rampart, and float boats on the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Wendi threatened invasion, Xu Sheng proposed a cordon from Jianye—palisades, fake towers, ships on the water.

sentences.zh: 諸將以爲無益，盛不聽，固立之。

translations.literal: The generals thought it useless; Sheng would not listen and firmly erected it.
translations.idiomatic: Other commanders scoffed; Xu Sheng built it anyway.

sentences.zh: 文帝到廣陵，望圍愕然，彌漫數百里，而江水盛長，便引軍退。

translations.literal: When Wendi reached Guangling, he looked on the enclosure startled—it stretched several hundred li—and the river water had risen high; then he led troops away.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangling Wei Wendi saw phantom ramparts for hundreds of li; high water blocked him and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 諸將乃伏。

translations.literal: The generals then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the skeptics concede.

sentences.zh: 〈干寶《晉紀》所云「疑城」，已注

translations.literal: (What Gan Bao's 《Jin ji》 calls the "doubtful walls" is already annotated
translations.idiomatic: (As Gan Bao's Jin ji labels the "illusory walls"—see the note

sentences.zh: 〈孫權傳〉。

translations.literal: in "Biography of Sun Quan."
translations.idiomatic: in the biography of Sun Quan.)

sentences.zh: 《魏氏春秋》云：文帝歎曰：「魏雖有武騎千羣，無所用也。」〉

translations.literal: 《Wei shi chunqiu》 says: Wendi sighed and said: "Though Wei has armored riders in thousands of squadrons, there is no use for them."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu records Wendi sighing that even thousands of Wei horsemen could not breach such defenses."

sentences.zh: 黃武中卒。

translations.literal: He died during the Huangwu era.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Huangwu reign.

sentences.zh: 子楷，襲爵領兵。

translations.literal: His son Kai inherited the noble rank and commanded troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kai inherited the fief and command.

sentences.zh: 潘璋字文珪，東郡發干人也。

translations.literal: Pan Zhang, courtesy name Wengui, was a man of Fagan in Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zhang, styled Wengui, came from Fagan in Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 孫權爲陽羨長，始往隨權。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan was chief of Yangxian, [Zhang] first went to follow Quan.
translations.idiomatic: He attached himself when Sun Quan governed Yangxian.

sentences.zh: 性博蕩嗜酒，居貧，好賒酤，債家至門，輒言後豪富相還。

translations.literal: By nature he was dissolute and fond of wine; he dwelt in poverty, loved to buy wine on credit; when creditors came to the door, he always said that later when rich and noble he would repay.
translations.idiomatic: He was wild, drank on credit, and told creditors he would pay when fortune came.

sentences.zh: 權奇愛之，因使召募，得百餘人，遂以爲將。

translations.literal: Quan marveled at and loved him; therefore he ordered him to recruit and obtained more than a hundred men; then he made him a general.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan liked his dash, let him raise a hundred men, and gave him a command.

sentences.zh: 討山賊有功，署別部司馬。

translations.literal: He campaigned against mountain bandits with merit and was appointed Major of a Separate Division.
translations.idiomatic: He earned major of a separate division clearing hill bandits.

sentences.zh: 後爲吳大巿刺姧，盜賊斷絕，由是知名，遷豫章西安長。

translations.literal: Later he became inspector of crime for Wu's great market; bandits and thieves were cut off; by this he became known and was transferred chief of Xi'an in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He policed Wu's market, stopped theft, became chief of Xi'an in Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 劉表在荊州，民數被寇，自璋在事，寇不入境。

translations.literal: While Liu Biao was in Jingzhou the people had repeatedly suffered raids; from the time Zhang held office raiders did not enter the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Under Liu Biao Xi'an had been raided constantly; Pan Zhang kept raiders out.

sentences.zh: 比縣建昌起爲賊亂，轉領建昌，加武猛校尉，討治惡民，旬月盡平，召合遺散，得八百人，將還建業。

translations.literal: Neighboring county Jianchang rose in bandit rebellion; he was transferred to hold Jianchang, advanced Colonel Who Displays Martial Ferocity, campaigned against and governed wicked people; within a month all was pacified; he summoned and gathered the scattered and obtained eight hundred men; he led them back to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianchang revolted he took the county, crushed outlaws in weeks, raised eight hundred men, and marched them to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 合肥之役，張遼奄至，諸將不備，陳武鬬死，宋謙、徐盛皆披走，璋身次在後，便馳進，橫馬斬謙、盛兵走者二人，兵皆還戰。

translations.literal: In the Hefei campaign Zhang Liao arrived suddenly; the various generals were unprepared; Chen Wu died fighting; Song Qian and Xu Sheng both fled in rout; Zhang's person was last in line; then he galloped forward, rode across and executed two fleeing soldiers of Qian and Sheng's troops; the soldiers all returned to fight.
translations.idiomatic: At Hefei Zhang Liao surprised them—Chen Wu fell, Song Qian and Xu Sheng broke—Pan Zhang rode up last, cut down two runners from their ranks, and rallied the line.

sentences.zh: 權甚壯之，拜偏將軍，遂領百校，屯半州。

translations.literal: Quan greatly honored him, appointed him Lieutenant General, then put him in charge of a hundred companies and garrisoned Banzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him lieutenant general, gave him a hundred companies, and posted him at Banzhou.

sentences.zh: 權征關羽，璋與朱然斷羽走道，到臨沮，住夾石。

translations.literal: When Quan campaigned against Guan Yu, Zhang together with Zhu Ran cut off Yu's escape route; reaching Linju they halted at Jiashi.
translations.idiomatic: Against Guan Yu he and Zhu Ran blocked retreat to Linju and Jiashi.

sentences.zh: 璋部下司馬馬忠禽羽，并羽子平、都督趙累等。

translations.literal: Zhang's division Major Ma Zhong captured Yu, together with Yu's son Ping and area commander Zhao Lei and others.
translations.idiomatic: Major Ma Zhong of his command seized Guan Yu, Guan Ping, and Zhao Lei.

sentences.zh: 權即分宜都巫、秭歸二縣爲固陵郡，拜璋爲太守、振威將軍，封溧陽侯。

translations.literal: Quan immediately partitioned Yidu's Wu and Zigui counties as Guling commandery, appointed Zhang prefect and General Who Shakes Might, and enfeoffed him marquis of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan carved Guling from Yidu, made Pan Zhang its prefect and shaking-might general, marquis of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 甘寧卒，又并其軍。

translations.literal: When Gan Ning died, he also absorbed his army.
translations.idiomatic: He absorbed Gan Ning's troops when Gan Ning died.

sentences.zh: 劉備出夷陵，璋與陸遜并力拒之，璋部下斬備護軍馮習等，所殺傷甚衆，拜平北將軍、襄陽太守。

translations.literal: When Liu Bei came out at Yiling, Zhang together with Lu Xun jointly resisted him; Zhang's subordinates beheaded Liu Bei's protector Feng Xi and others; those killed and wounded were very many; he was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Prefect of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Yiling he fought Lu Xun's battle, his men slew Feng Xi and many more; he became pacifying-north general and Xiangyang prefect.

sentences.zh: 魏將夏侯尚等圍南郡，分前部三萬人作浮橋，渡百里洲上，諸葛瑾、楊粲並會兵赴救，未知所出，而魏兵日渡不絕。

translations.literal: Wei general Xiahou Shang and others besieged Nan commandery; they divided thirty thousand men of the van to make a floating bridge and crossed onto Baili Isle; Zhuge Jin and Yang Can both gathered troops to rush relief but knew not what to do, while Wei troops crossed daily without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Shang bridged to Baili Isle with thirty thousand; Jin and Yang Can hesitated as Wei kept crossing.

sentences.zh: 璋曰：「魏勢始盛，江水又淺，未可與戰。

translations.literal: Zhang said: "Wei's momentum is just strong and the river water is shallow; we cannot yet fight them.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zhang said crossing now meant fighting Wei at peak strength in shallow water.

sentences.zh: 」便將所領，到魏上流五十里，伐葦數百萬束，縛作大筏，欲順流放火，燒敗浮橋。

translations.literal: " He then led those under his command fifty li upstream of Wei, cut several million bundles of reeds, bound them into great rafts, intending to float downstream and set fire to burn out the floating bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He moved fifty li upstream, bundled reeds into rafts, and planned to burn the pontoon from above.

sentences.zh: 作筏適畢，伺水長當下，尚便引退。

translations.literal: When the rafts were just finished, watching for the water to rise so as to go downstream, Shang then led away and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could launch, the river rose and Xiahou Shang withdrew.

sentences.zh: 璋下備陸口。

translations.literal: Zhang went down and garrisoned Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zhang then took station at Lukou.

sentences.zh: 權稱尊號，拜右將軍。

translations.literal: When Quan assumed the imperial title, he appointed Right General.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan became emperor he named Pan Zhang right general.

sentences.zh: 璋爲人麤猛，禁令肅然，好立功業，所領兵馬不過數千，而其所在常如萬人。

translations.literal: Zhang as a man was crude and fierce; prohibitions were austere; he loved to establish merit; the troops and horses he led did not exceed several thousand, yet wherever he was it was always as if there were ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zhang was harsh and few in men but hit like a division.

sentences.zh: 征伐止頓，便立軍巿，他軍所無，皆仰取足。

translations.literal: Wherever he campaigned and halted, he immediately established a military market; what other armies lacked, all looked to him to supply sufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Every halt sprouted an army market that supplied neighboring camps.

sentences.zh: 然性奢泰，末年彌甚，服物僭擬。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was extravagant; in his last years it grew extreme; clothing and goods presumptuously imitated [imperial style].
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he grew ostentatious and copied impermissible finery.

sentences.zh: 吏兵富者，或殺取其財物，數不奉法。

translations.literal: Among clerks and soldiers who were rich, some he killed and took their goods—several times he did not obey the law.
translations.idiomatic: He robbed wealthy subordinates and broke the law repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 監司舉奏，權惜其功而輒原不問。

translations.literal: Supervisors memorialized; Quan cherished his merit and always pardoned without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Censors reported him; Sun Quan forgave him for his record.

sentences.zh: 嘉禾三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Jiahe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jiahe 3.

sentences.zh: 子平，以無行徙會稽。

translations.literal: His son Ping, because of misconduct, was banished to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ping was banished to Kuaiji for bad conduct.

sentences.zh: 璋妻居建業，賜田宅，復客五十家。

translations.literal: Zhang's wife dwelt at Jianye; fields and houses were granted; fifty client households were restored.
translations.idiomatic: His widow stayed in Jianye with land, a house, and fifty client households.

sentences.zh: 丁奉字承淵，廬江安豐人也。

translations.literal: Ding Feng, courtesy name Chengyuan, was a man of Anfeng in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng, styled Chengyuan, came from Anfeng in Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 少以驍勇爲小將，屬甘寧、陸遜、潘璋等。

translations.literal: From youth as fierce bravery he was a minor general subordinate to Gan Ning, Lu Xun, Pan Zhang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He rose as a junior thunderbolt under Gan Ning, Lu Xun, and Pan Zhang.

sentences.zh: 數隨征伐，戰鬬常冠軍。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he followed on campaigns; in battle he constantly led the van.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned often and usually led the charge.

sentences.zh: 每斬將搴旗，身被創夷。

translations.literal: Whenever he beheaded generals and tore standards, his body suffered wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He took heads and flags and bore many wounds.

sentences.zh: 稍遷偏將軍。

translations.literal: Gradually he was promoted Lieutenant General.
translations.idiomatic: He rose stepwise to lieutenant general.

sentences.zh: 孫亮即位，爲冠軍將軍，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: When Sun Liang ascended the throne, he became General Who Surpasses All Champions and was enfeoffed village marquis of Ducheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sun Liang he became champion-surpassing general and village marquis at Ducheng.

sentences.zh: 魏遣諸葛誕、胡遵等攻東興，諸葛恪率軍拒之。

translations.literal: Wei sent Zhuge Dan, Hu Zun, and others to attack Dongxing; Zhuge Ke led the army to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei struck Dongxing; Zhuge Ke went to meet them.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「敵聞太傅自來，上岸必遁走。

translations.literal: The generals all said: "When the enemy hears the Grand Tutor has come in person, when they go ashore they will surely flee.
translations.idiomatic: His officers assumed Wei would bolt once Zhuge Ke landed.

sentences.zh: 」奉獨曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Feng alone said: "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng alone disagreed.

sentences.zh: 彼動其境內，悉許、洛兵大舉而來，必有成規，豈虛還哉？

translations.literal: They have stirred their whole territory and raised all the troops of Xu and Luoyang in a great expedition—they surely have a fixed plan; how could they return empty?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei had mobilized the heartland—this was no feint."

sentences.zh: 無恃敵之不至，恃吾有以勝之。

translations.literal: Do not rely on the enemy's not coming; rely on our having means to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Trust not that the foe stays away—trust preparation to beat him."

sentences.zh: 」及恪上岸，奉與將軍唐咨、呂據、留贊等，俱從山西上。

translations.literal: " When Ke went ashore, Feng together with generals Tang Zi, Lü Ju, Liu Zan, and others all ascended from the west of the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuge Ke landed, Ding Feng climbed the west hills with Tang Zi, Lü Ju, and Liu Zan.

sentences.zh: 奉曰：「今諸軍行遲，若敵據便地，則難與爭鋒矣。

translations.literal: Feng said: "Now the various armies march slowly; if the enemy seizes favorable ground, it will be hard to contend for the edge with them.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng warned that slow columns would cede the high ground.

sentences.zh: 」乃辟諸軍使下道，帥麾下三千人徑進。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he ordered the various armies to take the lower road and led three thousand men of his command straight forward.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the main body low while he took three thousand straight up.

sentences.zh: 時北風，奉舉帆二日至，遂據徐塘。

translations.literal: At the time there was a north wind; Feng raised sail and in two days arrived, then occupied Xu embankment.
translations.idiomatic: A north wind filled his sails; in two days he held Xu embankment.

sentences.zh: 天寒雪，敵諸將置酒高會，奉見其前部兵少，相謂曰：「取封侯爵賞，正在今日！

translations.literal: Heaven was cold with snow; the enemy generals set wine in high festivity; Feng saw their forward troops were few; they said to one another: "Taking marquis rank and rewards—just today!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei officers drank in the snow, blind to his approach—Ding Feng's men grinned that titles awaited them.

sentences.zh: 」乃使兵解鎧著冑，持短兵。

translations.literal: " He then ordered troops to remove armor and wear only helmets, wielding short weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered mail stripped for silent knives.

sentences.zh: 敵人從而笑焉，不爲設備。

translations.literal: The enemy followed and laughed at them; they did not prepare defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Wei laughed and stayed unready.

sentences.zh: 奉縱兵斫之，大破敵前屯。

translations.literal: Feng released troops to chop them; he greatly defeated the enemy's forward camp.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng's men hacked the forward camp apart.

sentences.zh: 會據等至，魏軍遂潰。

translations.literal: When Ju and others arrived, the Wei army then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Ju joined him Wei broke.

sentences.zh: 遷滅寇將軍，進封都鄉侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted General Who Extinguishes the Bandits and advanced enfeoffment to metropolitan village marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He became bandit-extinguishing general and metropolitan village marquis.

sentences.zh: 魏將文欽來降，以奉爲虎威將軍，從孫峻至壽春迎之，與敵追軍戰於高亭。

translations.literal: When Wei general Wen Qin came to surrender, [Sun Liang] appointed Feng General Who Displays Tiger Might; he followed Sun Jun to Shouchun to welcome him and fought the pursuing enemy army at Gaoting.
translations.idiomatic: He became tiger-might general, rode with Sun Jun to meet Wen Qin, and fought pursuers at Gaoting.

sentences.zh: 奉跨馬持矛，突入其陣中，斬首數百，獲其軍器。

translations.literal: Feng straddled a horse and held a spear, burst into their formation, beheaded several hundred, and captured their military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Wen Qin's pursuers with lance and horse, killing hundreds.

sentences.zh: 進封安豐侯。

translations.literal: He was advanced enfeoffment to marquis of Anfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to marquis of Anfeng.

sentences.zh: 太平二年，魏大將軍諸葛誕據壽春來降，魏人圍之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping, Wei Grand General Zhuge Dan held Shouchun and came over to surrender; Wei men besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping 2 Zhuge Dan defected at Shouchun and Wei besieged him.

sentences.zh: 遣朱異、唐咨等往救，復使奉與黎斐解圍。

translations.literal: He dispatched Zhu Yi, Tang Zi, and others to go relieve; again he ordered Feng together with Li Fei to lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent Zhu Yi and Tang Zi, then Ding Feng and Li Fei to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 奉爲先登，屯於黎漿，力戰有功，拜左將軍。

translations.literal: Feng was first to climb; he garrisoned at Lijiang; fighting hard he had merit; he was appointed Left General.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng spearheaded the relief at Lijiang and became left general.

sentences.zh: 孫休即位，與張布謀，欲誅孫綝，布曰：「丁奉雖不能吏書，而計略過人，能斷大事。

translations.literal: When Sun Xiu ascended the throne, together with Zhang Bu he plotted, wishing to execute Sun Lin; Bu said: "Though Ding Feng cannot clerk documents, his stratagem surpasses others and he can decide great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu conspired with Zhang Bu to kill Sun Lin; Zhang Bu called Ding Feng shrewd though barely literate.

sentences.zh: 」休召奉告曰：「綝秉國威，將行不軌，欲與將軍誅之。

translations.literal: " Xiu summoned Feng and informed him: "Lin holds the state's awesomeness and will act contrary to duty; I wish together with the general to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu told Ding Feng that Sun Lin must die.

sentences.zh: 」奉曰：「丞相兄弟友黨甚盛，恐人心不同，不可卒制，可因臘會，有陛下兵以誅之也。

translations.literal: " Feng said: "The Chancellor's brothers and friendly faction are very numerous; I fear hearts are not uniform and we cannot suddenly control them; we can use the year-end wax feast and employ Your Majesty's soldiers to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng proposed ambushing Sun Lin at the year-end feast with the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 」休納其計，因會請綝，奉與張布目左右斬之。

translations.literal: " Xun accepted his plan; by the feast he invited Lin; Feng together with Zhang Bu signaled those to left and right and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: At the feast Ding Feng and Zhang Bu's guards struck Sun Lin down.

sentences.zh: 遷大將軍，加左右都護。

translations.literal: He was promoted Grand General and added concurrent Left and Right Protectors.
translations.idiomatic: He became grand general with dual protector posts.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，假節領徐州牧。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongan he held credentials and concurrently acted Shepherds of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongan 2 he bore credentials as acting Xuzhou shepherd.

sentences.zh: 六年，魏伐蜀，奉率諸軍向壽春，爲救蜀之勢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Wei attacked Shu; Feng led the various armies toward Shouchun, making a posture of relieving Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 Wei invaded Shu; Ding Feng feigned a thrust at Shouchun to distract Wei.

sentences.zh: 蜀亡，軍還。

translations.literal: When Shu perished, the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu fell the force marched home.

sentences.zh: 休薨，奉與丞相濮陽興等從萬彧之言，共迎立孫皓，遷右大司馬左軍師。

translations.literal: When Xiu died, Feng together with Chancellor Puyang Xing and others following Wan Yu's words jointly welcomed and established Sun Hao; he was promoted Grand Marshal of the Right and Left Army Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Xiu he backed Puyang Xing and Wan Yu in raising Sun Hao—grand marshal right and army mentor.

sentences.zh: 寶鼎三年，皓命奉與諸葛靚攻合肥。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, Hao ordered Feng together with Zhuge Jing to attack Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 3 Sun Hao sent Ding Feng and Zhuge Jing against Hefei.

sentences.zh: 奉與晉大將石苞書，搆而間之，苞以徵還。

translations.literal: Feng wrote to Jin Grand General Shi Bao, slandering to sow discord; Bao was summoned back by investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Feng wrote Jin's Shi Bao into recall with rumor and intrigue.

sentences.zh: 建衡元年，奉復帥衆治徐塘，因攻晉穀陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianheng, Feng again led the multitude to work Xu embankment; then he attacked Jin's Guyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianheng 1 he reworked Xu embankment and raided Jin's Guyang.

sentences.zh: 穀陽民知之，引去，奉無所獲。

translations.literal: The people of Guyang knew it and withdrew; Feng obtained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Guyang emptied before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 皓怒，斬奉導軍。

translations.literal: Hao was angry and executed Feng's guide-general.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hao executed his column guide for the failure.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year.

sentences.zh: 奉貴而有功，漸以驕矜，或有毀之者，皓追以前出軍事，徙奉家於臨川。

translations.literal: Feng was noble and had merit; gradually he grew arrogant; some slandered him; Hao traced earlier military affairs and moved Feng's household to Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Once proud and exposed, slander and old faults sent his clan to Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 奉弟封，官至後將軍，先奉死。

translations.literal: Younger brother Ding Feng held the rank of Rear General and died before Ding Feng (Chengyuan).
translations.idiomatic: His junior brother Ding Feng served as rear general but predeceased him (both brothers' names are romanized Ding Feng in modern Mandarin).

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：凡此諸將，皆江表之虎臣，孫氏之所厚待也。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: All these generals were tiger ministers east of the Yangzi; they were those whom the Sun clan richly favored.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: These commanders were Wu's iron champions—the men the Suns favored.

sentences.zh: 以潘璋之不脩，權能忘過記功，其保據東南，宜哉！

translations.literal: As for Pan Zhang's want of self-cultivation, that Quan could forget faults and record merit—his preserving and holding the southeast was fitting indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan overlooked Pan Zhang's excess to reward talent—small wonder he held the southeast.

sentences.zh: 陳表將家支庶，而與胄子名人比翼齊衡，拔萃出類，不亦美乎！

translations.literal: Chen Biao, though a junior branch of a general's house, stood wing to wing with heirs of famous houses and sons of high lineage—surpassing the crowd and standing out—was it not beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: Chen Biao rose from a cadet line to walk beside great heirs—a splendid exception."
